1│ """The online engine: a bounded working context over an unbounded conversation.
     2│ 
     3│ A conversation can grow to millions of tokens; no model reads that much per
     4│ request, and none needs to. The engine keeps two things apart:
     5│ 
     6│   * the *memory*: every message, processed once when it arrives (provenance
     7│     trace, chunk features, an inverted index of the chunks' topic words).
     8│     Nothing is recomputed per request, so the cost of a request does not grow
     9│     with the length of the history;
    10│   * the *view*: what is sent for the next model call. The first message is
    11│     kept as the anchor, the recent messages are kept whole, and in between the
    12│     learned model decides paragraph by paragraph what stays (``learn.py``).
    13│     When the view passes ``cap`` tokens the oldest messages leave it entirely
    14│     and a short map of them (the requests made, the files changed) is attached
    15│     to the anchor. Between those moments the view only grows at the end, so
    16│     the provider's prompt cache keeps hitting.
    17│ 
    18│ What leaves the view is not lost. At every request the index shortlists, among
    19│ everything out of view, the chunks that share the rarest words with what is
    20│ about to be sent (BM25 over the postings of those words only, so a search
    21│ costs about the same at ten thousand chunks as at ten million tokens), the
    22│ ``soon`` head of the model re-ranks them, and the ones likely to be needed now
    23│ are appended to the request, within a token budget ("tweezers").
    24│ 
    25│ The offline evaluation (``learn.Learned``) drives this same class step by
    26│ step, so what is measured on recorded sessions is what runs in the proxy.
    27│ """
    28│

    70│ def key_lines(lines: list[str], k: int) -> list[str]:
    71│     """The ``k`` lines that name the most distinctive things (paths, identifiers, values), in their order,
    72│     shortened. A pure function of the lines, so a stub shows the same bytes on every request."""
    73│     scored = sorted(((len(words(ln)), -i) for i, ln in enumerate(lines) if ln.strip()), reverse=True)[:k]
    74│     keep = sorted(-i for n, i in scored if n)
    75│     return [lines[i] if len(lines[i]) <= 160 else lines[i][:159] + "…" for i in keep]

    78│ def at_birth(m: dict, stages: frozenset) -> dict:
    79│     """``m`` as the model will see it from the moment it arrives (copy-on-write). ``squeeze``: tool outputs
    80│     through the mechanical squeezer; ``telegraph``: filler words out of the prose the person and the harness
    81│     write; ``telegraph-agent``: also out of the agent's own text. Both are pure functions of the message,
    82│     so the result is the same on every request and the prompt cache is unaffected: unlike a later cut,
    83│     shrinking a message before it is first sent costs nothing."""
    84│     if not stages:
    85│         return m
    86│     content = m.get("content")
    87│     prose = "telegraph" in stages and (m.get("role") == "user" or "telegraph-agent" in stages)
    88│     if isinstance(content, str):
    89│         return dict(m, content=compress(content)) if prose and compress(content) != content else m
    90│     if not isinstance(content, list):
    91│         return m
    92│     out, changed = [], False
    93│     for b in content:
    94│         nb = b
    95│         if isinstance(b, dict):
    96│             t = b.get("type")
    97│             if t == "tool_result" and "squeeze" in stages:
    98│                 c = b.get("content")
    99│                 if isinstance(c, str):
   100│                     sq = squeeze(c)
   101│                     nb = dict(b, content=sq) if sq != c else b
   102│                 elif isinstance(c, list):
   103│                     parts = [dict(x, text=squeeze(x["text"])) if isinstance(x, dict) and x.get("type") == "text"
   104│                              and isinstance(x.get("text"), str) and squeeze(x["text"]) != x["text"] else x for x in c]
   105│                     nb = dict(b, content=parts) if any(x is not y for x, y in zip(parts, c)) else b
   106│             elif t == "text" and prose and isinstance(b.get("text"), str):
   107│                 tc = compress(b["text"])
   108│                 nb = dict(b, text=tc) if tc != b["text"] else b
   109│         changed |= nb is not b
   110│         out.append(nb)
   111│     return dict(m, content=out) if changed else m

   114│ class ChunkIndex:
   115│     """Inverted index of chunk topic words. A search reads only the postings of the query's rarest words,
   116│     which are short: its cost depends on how specific the query is, not on how much is indexed."""
   117│ 
   118│     def __init__(self):
   119│         self.ids: dict[str, int] = {}
   120│         self.postings: list[array] = []
   121│         self.chunks: list[tuple[int, int]] = []  # chunk id -> (unit, chunk number)
   122│         self.lengths = array("I")
   123│         self.total = 0
   124│ 
   125│     def add(self, unit: int, j: int, terms, tokens: int) -> int:
   126│         cid = len(self.chunks)
   127│         self.chunks.append((unit, j))
   128│         self.lengths.append(tokens)
   129│         self.total += tokens
   130│         for w in terms:
   131│             k = self.ids.get(w)
   132│             if k is None:
   133│                 k = self.ids[w] = len(self.postings)
   134│                 self.postings.append(array("I"))
   135│             self.postings[k].append(cid)
   136│         return cid
   137│ 
   138│     def search(self, weights: dict, k: int, accept, max_terms: int = 24) -> list[tuple[float, int]]:
   139│         """Best ``k`` accepted chunks by BM25 (binary term frequency) for ``weights`` (word -> idf),
   140│         using the ``max_terms`` heaviest words."""
   141│         if not self.chunks:
   142│             return []
   143│         terms = heapq.nlargest(max_terms, ((w, t) for t, w in weights.items() if t in self.ids))
   144│         acc: Counter = Counter()
   145│         for w, t in terms:
   146│             for cid in self.postings[self.ids[t]]:
   147│                 acc[cid] += w
   148│         if not acc:
   149│             return []
   150│         avg, lengths = self.total / len(self.chunks), self.lengths
   151│         scored = ((s * 2.2 / (1 + 1.2 * (0.25 + 0.75 * lengths[c] / avg)), c) for c, s in acc.items())
   152│         out = []
   153│         for s, c in heapq.nlargest(k * 4 + 64, scored):
   154│             if accept(c):
   155│                 out.append((s, c))
   156│                 if len(out) == k:
   157│                     break
   158│         return out
   159│

   161│ class Engine:
   162│     """Curation of one conversation, message by message. ``sync`` takes in the messages the conversation
   163│     has gained; ``view`` returns what to send for the next model call.
   164│ 
   165│     Parameters of the learned policy: ``threshold`` (chunks the ``keep`` head scores below it may be
   166│     dropped), ``protect`` (the latest messages are never touched), ``check`` (re-score after this many
   167│     tokens of growth), ``recall``/``budget``/``shortlist`` (tweezers: probability of use soon needed to
   168│     bring a chunk back, tokens per request, candidates re-ranked), ``ratio`` (price of cached input),
   169│     ``horizon``/``margin`` (the cost model of a cut). ``rank``: recall order, ``soon`` (the ``soon`` head, ``recall`` its minimum) or ``words`` (BM25 to the
   170│     request; ``recall`` is then only a floor on the ``soon`` head). ``rule``: when to rewrite, ``rent`` (rent or
   171│     buy, ``_rent``; ``trust`` < 1 lets the predicted length of the segment move the moment, ``every``: requests
   172│     between two looks) or ``gain`` (the saving forecast over ``horizon``). ``ttl``: seconds the provider keeps
   173│     the cache (0: forever); after a longer pause the request is paid in full anyway, so the engine cleans up
   174│     then. ``birth``: what ``at_birth`` does to each message as it arrives (``squeeze+telegraph``). ``stub``:
   175│     what a removed paragraph leaves (``plain`` marker, or its ``lines`` with the most names). ``cap``:
   176│     maximum tokens of messages in the view
   177│     (0: no cap); when passed, the oldest messages leave the view until it is under ``floor`` × ``cap``.
   178│     ``eoq``: the cap set by the economic order quantity instead (``_eoq_cap``): after a rewrite the view goes
   179│     down to ``eoq`` tokens. ``ledger``: tokens of the anchor given to the lines of the messages that left whose
   180│     names are most likely to be needed again (``ledger.py``)."""
   181│ 
   182│     def __init__(self, model: Model, threshold: float = 0.3, protect: int = 6, check: int = 4000,
   183│                  recall: float = 0.0, budget: int = 1500, ratio: float = 0.1, horizon: int = 10,
   184│                  margin: float = 1.0, shortlist: int = 40, cap: int = 0, floor: float = 0.6, rank: str = "soon",
   185│                  rule: str = "rent", trust: float = 1.0, every: int = 4, ttl: float = 0.0, birth: str = "",
   186│                  stub: str = "plain", head: str = "keep", miss: int = 0, early: float = 0.0, spill: str = "",
   187│                  terms: int = 24, cold: int = 0, eoq: int = 0, ledger: int = 0, least: float = 0.0005,
   188│                  outcome: str = "head", gwin: int = 0, lerr: float = 0.0, jit: int = 0):
   189│         self._params = dict(threshold=threshold, protect=protect, check=check, recall=recall, budget=budget,
   190│                             ratio=ratio, horizon=horizon, margin=margin, shortlist=shortlist, cap=cap, floor=floor,
   191│                             rank=rank, rule=rule, trust=trust, every=every, ttl=ttl, birth=birth, stub=stub, head=head,
   192│                             miss=miss, early=early, spill=spill, terms=terms, cold=cold, eoq=eoq, ledger=ledger,
   193│                             least=least, outcome=outcome, gwin=gwin, lerr=lerr, jit=jit)
   194│         # ``jit``: tokens per request of just-in-time lines: lines of the messages that left the view that share a
   195│         # name with what has just arrived (the file being edited, the error just raised) and hold names the view
   196│         # lacks, appended to the latest message (``_jit_text``); 0: off
   197│         self.jit = jit
   198│         self._jit: dict[int, str] = {}  # message -> the lines appended to it, fixed once written (the cache)
   199│         self._jit_lines: dict[int, set] = {}  # message -> the (message, line) ids of those lines
   200│         self._ledger_ids: set = set()  # (message, line) in the ledger now
   201│         self._jit_ids: set = set()  # (message, line) appended to messages still in view
   202│         self._tags: dict[tuple, frozenset] = {}  # (message, line) of a tool result -> the names of its call
   203│         # ``lerr``: the ledger prior's weight on names that failure reports (errors, failed tests) named: the
   204│         # "why" of a fix (0: the prior as calibrated)
   205│         self.lerr = lerr
   206│         # ``gwin``: the EOQ's growth per call ``g`` measured over the last ``gwin`` calls (0: the whole session)
   207│         self.gwin = gwin
   208│         # ``outcome``: what of the agent's closing reply to a request the map keeps once the reply has left the
   209│         # view: its first OUTCOME_CHARS ("head"), the lines naming the most files, functions and values
   210│         # ("lines"), or nothing ("none"). On the unseen recorded segments, in one run: 63.9% without it, 63.6%
   211│         # with the head, 63.4% with the lines; the head stays, for what the simulation cannot see (live, the
   212│         # marathon's last request took 5 calls instead of 40). Telegraphing the reply changed nothing.
   213│         self.outcome = outcome
   214│         self.eoq = eoq
   215│         self.ledger, self.least = ledger, least
   216│         self._names = None  # what is known of every name (``ledger.Names``), with ``ledger``
   217│         self._pool: list[tuple] = []  # (message, line, names) of the messages that left the view
   218│         self.ledger_text = ""  # the ledger the anchor carries now
   219│         self.head_tokens = 0  # the system prompt and tool definitions sent with every request (set by the caller)
   220│         # ``cold``: when the provider's cache has expired the whole request is paid in full anyway, so the view
   221│         # is rebuilt down to this many tokens for free (0: only what scores low goes)
   222│         self.cold = cold
   223│         # ``terms``: words of what is about to be sent that recall searches with, the rarest first. The rarest
   224│         # ones are often only in the latest messages, which are in view: too few find nothing out of view
   225│         self.terms = terms
   226│         # ``spill``: a directory where every message is also written, one file per message, as it came; whatever
   227│         # leaves the view says where its full text is, so the agent can always read it back with one call
   228│         self.spill, self._spill_dir = spill, None
   229│         # ``early`` > 0: paragraphs of a block the agent has seen once whose probability of later use is below it
   230│         # are cut at the next request, when cutting costs almost nothing (``_cut_early``)
   231│         self.early = early
   232│         # with ``miss`` > 0, a chunk of n tokens is recalled when p · (n + miss) > n: when what its absence is
   233│         # expected to cost (reading it again and one more model call, ``miss`` tokens) exceeds sending it now
   234│         self.miss = miss
   235│         # what a paragraph must be likely to be used for to stay: "keep" (at this step or later) or "turn"
   236│         # (before the person's next request: what the request in progress needs; later needs are recalled)
   237│         self.head = head
   238│         self._prob = model.turn_prob if head == "turn" else model.prob
   239│         self.stub = stub  # what a removed paragraph leaves behind: "plain" (a marker) or "lines" (its key lines)
   240│         self.birth = frozenset(x for x in birth.replace(",", "+").split("+") if x)
   241│         self._last_raw: dict | None = None  # the last message as received (before at_birth), to check the history
   242│         self.rank = rank  # recall order: "soon" (probability of use soon) or "words" (BM25 to the request)
   243│         self.rule, self.trust, self.every, self.ttl = rule, trust, every, ttl
   244│         self.model, self.threshold, self.protect, self.check = model, threshold, protect, check
   245│         self.recall = recall if model.soon else 0.0
   246│         self.budget, self.ratio, self.horizon, self.margin, self.shortlist = budget, ratio, horizon, margin, shortlist
   247│         self.cap, self.floor = cap, floor
   248│         self.tracer = Tracer()
   249│         self.tr = self.tracer.tr
   250│         self.fz = Featurizer(self.tr)
   251│         self.index = ChunkIndex()
   252│         self.cid: dict[tuple[int, int], int] = {}  # (unit, chunk) -> chunk id
   253│         self.sizes: list[int] = []  # tokens of each message as received
   254│         self.raw_tokens = 0
   255│         self.dropped: dict[int, set] = {}  # unit -> chunks replaced by a marker
   256│         self.recalled: dict[int, list] = {}  # message -> (unit, chunk) appended to it
   257│         self.live: set = set()  # chunks appended somewhere
   258│         self.start = 1  # messages[1:start] have left the view
   259│         self.map_text = ""  # what the anchor says about them
   260│         self._gone = Counter()  # files changed in them (path -> times)
   261│         self.gone_tokens = self.gone_commands = 0
   262│         self.checked = 0  # view size at the last scoring
   263│         self.notes: dict[int, str] = {}  # message -> text appended to it (loop warnings, recalled facts)
   264│         self._built: dict[int, tuple] = {}  # message -> (key, message as sent, tokens)
   265│         self.born: dict[int, int] = {}  # unit -> model calls made before it arrived
   266│         self.held: dict[tuple, float] = {}  # (unit, chunk) proposed for removal -> rent paid on it so far
   267│         self.held_at = 0  # model calls made when the rent was last brought up to date
   268│         self.checked_at = 0  # ... when the view was last scored
   269│         self.last_at: float | None = None  # when the last request was sent (seconds)
   270│         self.probe: tuple | None = None  # see _rent
   271│         self.stats = Counter()

   273│     # ------------------------------------------------------------ memory
   274│ 
   275│     @property
   276│     def msgs(self) -> list[dict]:
   277│         return self.tr.msgs
   278│ 
   279│     def add(self, m: dict) -> None:
   280│         m = af.strip_cache_control(m)
   281│         self._last_raw = m
   282│         if self.spill:
   283│             self._write_spill(len(self.tr.msgs), m)
   284│         if self.birth:
   285│             m = at_birth(m, self.birth)
   286│             self.stats["birth_saved"] += max(0, est(self._last_raw) - est(m))
   287│         self.tracer.add(m)
   288│         self.sizes.append(est(m))
   289│         self.raw_tokens += self.sizes[-1]
   290│         for i in self.fz.extend():
   291│             self.born[i] = len(self.tr.steps)
   292│             u = self.tr.units[i]
   293│             if u.kind == "thinking" or not u.msg or not (u.saving or u.kind in ("user", "text")):
   294│                 continue
   295│             # what can leave the view is indexed, so that it can come back: tool outputs, long inputs (written
   296│             # content, long commands), and the person's and the agent's words (a short call, such as the path
   297│             # given to a read, would only crowd out its own result)
   298│             for j, c in enumerate(self.fz.chunks(i)):
   299│                 self.cid[(i, j)] = self.index.add(i, j, c.terms, self._chunk_tokens(i, j))

   301│     def spill_path(self, mi: int) -> str:
   302│         """Where message ``mi`` (counted from 0) is kept on disk ("" without ``spill``): named by its number
   303│         counted from 1, as the anchor and the cards name messages."""
   304│         return os.path.join(self._spill_dir, f"m{mi + 1:05d}.md") if self._spill_dir else ""
   305│ 
   306│     def _write_spill(self, mi: int, m: dict) -> None:
   307│         if self._spill_dir is None:  # the first message names the conversation
   308│             self._spill_dir = os.path.join(os.path.expanduser(self.spill), af.sha(af.canonical(m))[:12])
   309│             os.makedirs(self._spill_dir, exist_ok=True)
   310│         parts = [f"# message {mi + 1} ({m.get('role')})"]
   311│         for b in af.blocks(m.get("content")):
   312│             t = b.get("type") if isinstance(b, dict) else None
   313│             if t == "text":
   314│                 parts.append(b.get("text", ""))
   315│             elif t == "tool_use":
   316│                 parts.append(f"[call {b.get('name')}] " + json.dumps(b.get("input"), ensure_ascii=False, indent=1))
   317│             elif t == "tool_result":
   318│                 parts.append(f"[result]\n{af.text_of(b.get('content'))}")
   319│             elif t in ("image", "document"):
   320│                 parts.append(f"[{t}]")
   321│         with open(self.spill_path(mi), "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
   322│             f.write("\n\n".join(parts) + "\n")

   324│     def sync(self, msgs: list[dict], trusted: bool = False) -> bool:
   325│         """Takes in ``msgs[len(self.msgs):]``. Unless ``trusted`` (the caller verified that the history
   326│         only grew), the last known message is compared first; if the history was rewritten the engine
   327│         starts over. Returns False when it started over."""
   328│         n = len(self.msgs)
   329│         fresh = True
   330│         if n and (len(msgs) < n or (not trusted and af.strip_cache_control(msgs[n - 1]) != self._last_raw)):

   339│     def view(self, now: float | None = None) -> list[dict]:

   349│     def position(self, mi: int) -> int | None:

   362│     def decide(self, now: float | None = None) -> None:
   363│         """Drops, moves out and recalls what the next model call should (not) see."""

   366│             return
   367│         k = len(self.tr.steps)

   369│         if now is not None:
   370│             self.last_at = now
   371│         sizes = self._sizes()
   372│         total = sum(sizes)
   373│         first = None
   374│         if self.early and k >= 2:
   375│             self._cut_early(t)
   376│             sizes = self._sizes()
   377│             total = sum(sizes)
   378│         due = total - self.checked >= self.check or (self.rule == "rent" and k - self.checked_at >= self.every)
   379│         if self.eoq:
   380│             self.cap, self.floor = self._eoq_cap(k)
   381│         if (self.cap and total > self.cap) or (cold and k):
   382│             # Over the cap the context is rewritten anyway, and once the provider's cache has expired the
   383│             # whole request is paid in full anyway: every low-scoring chunk goes, and if the view is still
   384│             # too large the oldest messages leave.
   385│             first = self._evict(t, k, sizes, free=True)
   386│             sizes = self._sizes()

   388│                 if (self.cap or (cold and self.cold)) else 0

   390│                 first = 1

   393│             first = self._evict(t, k, sizes)

   395│             for m in [m for m in self.recalled if m >= first]:
   396│                 self.live.difference_update(self.recalled.pop(m))
   397│         if first is not None or due or cold:
   398│             self.checked, self.checked_at = sum(self._sizes()), k
   399│         if self.jit and self._pool and t - 1 not in self._jit:
   400│             self._jit_text(t)

   404│                 self.recalled[t - 1] = picked
   405│                 self.live.update(picked)
   406│                 self.stats["recalled_chunks"] += len(picked)
   407│                 self.stats["recalled_tokens"] += sum(self._chunk_tokens(i, j) for i, j in picked)

   409│     def _eoq_cap(self, k: int) -> tuple[int, float]:
   410│         """The cap and floor of the economic order quantity. A rewrite down to ``K`` tokens (``eoq``) sends those
   411│         ``K`` anew: it costs ``(1 - ratio) * K`` more than reading them from the cache (the head, the system
   412│         prompt and tools before the messages, is a prefix the rewrite does not touch: it stays cached, as the
   413│         live requests show). Between two rewrites the view grows from ``K`` by ``Q``, ``g`` tokens per model
   414│         call, and every call re-reads it at ``ratio``. Per call, ``ratio * (K + Q / 2) + (1 - ratio) * K * g /
   415│         Q``, which is least at ``Q* = sqrt(2 (1 - ratio) K g / ratio)``: rewriting more often pays the rewrite
   416│         too often, less often re-reads too much. ``g`` is what this conversation has added per call."""
   417│         if self.ratio <= 0:
   418│             return 0, self.floor  # reading the cache is free: no reason to rewrite
   419│         if self.gwin and k > self.gwin:  # what the last ``gwin`` calls added
   420│             g = sum(self.sizes[self.tr.steps[k - self.gwin]:]) / self.gwin
   421│         else:
   422│             g = self.raw_tokens / max(1, k)
   423│         q = math.sqrt(2 * (1 - self.ratio) * self.eoq * g / self.ratio) if self.ratio < 1 else 0
   424│         cap = int(self.eoq + q) or 1
   425│         return cap, self.eoq / cap

   427│     def _visible(self) -> range | list:

   437│     def _key(self, mi: int) -> tuple:

   441│             ((self.notes[mi],) if mi in self.notes else ()) + ((self._jit[mi],) if mi in self._jit else ())

   443│     def _message(self, mi: int) -> tuple[dict, int]:

   473│     def later(self, k: int) -> float:
   474│         """Expected number of further requests after step ``k`` (see ``learn.Learned.later``)."""

   477│     def _cut_early(self, t: int) -> None:
   478│         """Cuts where it is cheapest. A tool output the agent saw at the previous request (and the content it
   479│         wrote one exchange earlier) is followed only by messages that were never cached, so cutting it now
   480│         costs about its own cached price, once; later the price grows with everything sent after it. What
   481│         the agent did with it is known by now, which is what the ``early`` head judges."""
   482│         steps = self.tr.steps
   483│         lo, hi = steps[-2], steps[-1]  # messages the request before last showed for the first time
   484│         ctx = None
   485│         for mi in range(lo, hi):
   486│             for i in self.fz.by_msg.get(mi, ()):
   487│                 u = self.tr.units[i]
   488│                 if not u.saving or u.kind not in ("result", "call"):
   489│                     continue
   490│                 ctx = ctx or self.fz.context(t)
   491│                 have = self.dropped.get(i, set())
   492│                 drop = {j for j, c in enumerate(self.fz.chunks(i))
   493│                         if j not in have and self.model.early_prob(self.fz.vector(c, ctx)) < self.early}
   494│                 if drop:
   495│                     self.dropped[i] = have | drop
   496│                     self.stats["early_chunks"] += len(drop)

   499│     def _candidates(self, t: int):

   507│     def _evict(self, t: int, k: int, sizes: list[int], free: bool = False) -> int | None:
   508│         """Drops what scores low where that pays most. Removing content from message ``f`` on sends
   509│         everything after ``f`` uncached once, while each later request saves the cached price of what
   510│         is removed. Every ``f`` is tried; the best one is applied if its net saving is positive. With
   511│         ``free`` the context is being sent anew anyway, so every low-scoring chunk goes. Returns ``f``."""
   512│         ctx = self.fz.context(t)
   513│         proposal = []  # (message, unit, chunks, tokens)
   514│         for i in self._candidates(t):
   515│             have = self.dropped.get(i, set())
   516│             chunks = self.fz.chunks(i)
   517│             if len(have) == len(chunks):
   518│                 continue
   519│             more = {j for j, c in enumerate(chunks)
   520│                     if j not in have and self._low(self._prob(self.fz.vector(c, ctx)), c.tokens)}
   521│             if more:
   522│                 proposal.append((self.tr.units[i].msg, i, more, sum(chunks[j].tokens for j in more)))
   523│         if not proposal:
   524│             self.held, self.held_at = {}, k
   525│             return None
   526│         if free:
   527│             best_at = 0
   528│         elif self.rule == "rent":

   530│             if best_at is None:
   531│                 return None
   532│         else:
   533│             cum = [0]
   534│             for s in sizes:
   535│                 cum.append(cum[-1] + s)
   536│             later = self.ratio * self.later(k)
   537│             best, best_at, saved = 0.0, None, 0
   538│             for n in range(len(proposal) - 1, -1, -1):  # cut points from the most recent backwards
   539│                 saved += proposal[n][3]
   540│                 f = proposal[n][0]
   541│                 if n and proposal[n - 1][0] == f:
   542│                     continue
   543│                 net = later * saved - self.margin * (1 - self.ratio) * (cum[t] - cum[f] - saved)
   544│                 if net > best:
   545│                     best, best_at = net, n
   546│             if best_at is None:
   547│                 return None
   548│         for _, i, more, tokens in proposal[best_at:]:
   549│             self.dropped[i] = self.dropped.get(i, set()) | more
   550│             self.stats["dropped_chunks"] += len(more)
   551│             for j in more:
   552│                 self.held.pop((i, j), None)
   553│         if free:
   554│             self.held, self.held_at = {}, k
   555│         self.stats["rewrites"] += 1
   556│         return proposal[best_at][0]
   557│ 
   558│     def _low(self, p: float, tokens: int) -> bool:
   559│         """Whether a chunk scores low enough to go."""
   560│         return p < self.threshold

   562│     def _rent(self, t: int, k: int, sizes: list[int], proposal: list) -> int | None:
   563│         """Rent or buy. Every request that carries a chunk proposed for removal pays its cached price
   564│         (the rent); removing the chunks from message ``f`` on costs, once, the rest of the context from
   565│         ``f`` on sent again uncached (the price). A cut is bought once the rent already paid on what it
   566│         removes reaches its price (``hindsight.rent_threshold``: scaled by the predicted length of the
   567│         segment when ``trust`` < 1); of those, the one that removes most. Unlike a forecast of the
   568│         savings, this needs no estimate of how long the session will go on to stay within a constant
   569│         factor of the best schedule at a fixed price (here the price grows with what is sent after the cut,
   570│         and the cap bounds the loss). The price counts only what was sent before: the messages since the
   571│         last request (the agent's reply and its results) are paid in full either way. Extending a cut
   572│         further back must be paid by the rent of the chunks it adds, not by the rent already spent on a
   573│         nearer cut. Returns the index in ``proposal`` of the first chunk removed."""
   574│         from .hindsight import rent_threshold
   575│         held, since = {}, self.held_at
   576│         for _, i, more, _ in proposal:  # bring the rent up to date (chunks proposed now, since the last count)
   577│             chunks, age = self.fz.chunks(i), k - max(since, self.born.get(i, 0))
   578│             for j in more:
   579│                 held[(i, j)] = self.held.get((i, j), 0.0) + self.ratio * chunks[j].tokens * max(0, age)
   580│         self.held, self.held_at = held, k
   581│         cum = [0]
   582│         for s in sizes:
   583│             cum.append(cum[-1] + s)
   584│         lengths = self.model.trained_on.get("lengths") or []
   585│         sent = min(t, self.tr.steps[-1]) if self.tr.steps else t  # messages before this were sent before
   586│         best_at, saved, paid, bought = None, 0, 0.0, (0.0, 0.0)
   587│         self.probe = None  # the cut closest to being bought: (message, tokens, rent paid, rent needed)
   588│         for n in range(len(proposal) - 1, -1, -1):  # cut points from the most recent backwards
   589│             _, i, more, tokens = proposal[n]
   590│             saved += tokens
   591│             paid += sum(held[(i, j)] for j in more)
   592│             f = proposal[n][0]
   593│             if n and proposal[n - 1][0] == f:
   594│                 continue
   595│             price = self.margin * (1 - self.ratio) * max(0, cum[sent] - cum[min(f, sent)] - saved)
   596│             need = rent_threshold(self.trust, lengths, k, price, self.ratio * saved) * price
   597│             if paid >= need and paid - bought[0] >= need - bought[1]:  # the extension pays for itself
   598│                 best_at, bought = n, (paid, need)
   599│             if self.probe is None or paid / max(need, 1e-9) > self.probe[2] / max(self.probe[3], 1e-9):
   600│                 self.probe = (f, saved, paid, need)
   601│         return best_at
   602│ 
   603│     def _leave(self, sizes: list[int], target: float | None = None) -> bool:
   604│         """Moves the oldest messages out of the view until it is under ``target`` (``floor`` × ``cap``). The
   605│         view must go on with an assistant message after the anchor (the removed messages take their tool
   606│         calls and results with them). Returns False when nothing can leave (all of it is recent)."""
   607│         t = len(self.msgs)
   608│         target = self.floor * self.cap if target is None else target
   609│         total, new_start = sum(sizes), self.start
   610│         mi = self.start
   611│         while mi < min(t - self.protect, t - 1) and total > target:
   612│             total -= sizes[mi]
   613│             mi += 1
   614│             if self.msgs[mi]["role"] == "assistant":
   615│                 new_start = mi
   616│         if new_start == self.start:
   617│             return False
   618│         for mi in range(self.start, new_start):
   619│             self.gone_tokens += self.sizes[mi]
   620│             for i in self.fz.by_msg.get(mi, ()):
   621│                 cat, path, _ = self.fz.info.get(i, ("", None, False))
   622│                 if self.tr.units[i].kind == "call" and cat == WRITE and path:
   623│                     self._gone[path] += 1

   625│                     self.gone_commands += 1
   626│                     for w in shell_writes(str((_block(self.tr, i).get("input") or {}).get("command", ""))):
   627│                         self._gone[w] += 1
   628│         self.stats["left_messages"] += new_start - self.start
   629│         if self.ledger:
   630│             from .ledger import POOL, lines_of
   631│             for mi in range(self.start, new_start):
   632│                 for i in self.fz.by_msg.get(mi, ()):
   633│                     u = self.tr.units[i]
   634│                     if u.kind == "thinking":
   635│                         continue
   636│                     lines = lines_of(unit_text(self.tr, i), words)
   637│                     if self.jit and u.kind == "result":  # the lines of a result are reached through its call's
   638│                         tag = self._call_words(i)  # names (the file read, the command run): ``_jit_text``
   639│                         if tag:
   640│                             for ln, _ in lines:
   641│                                 self._tags[(mi, ln)] = tag
   642│                     self._pool += [(mi, ln, ws) for ln, ws in lines]
   643│             del self._pool[:-POOL]
   644│             if len(self._tags) > 2 * POOL:
   645│                 keep = {(mi, ln) for mi, ln, _ in self._pool}
   646│                 self._tags = {k: v for k, v in self._tags.items() if k in keep}
   647│         self.start = new_start
   648│         self.map_text = self._map()

   650│             # the ledger is part of the view it leaves behind: never more than 80% of it, or the view would be
   651│             # over its target again at once and every request would rewrite it
   652│             text = self._ledger_text(min(self.ledger, int(0.8 * target)))
   653│             self.ledger_text = text
   654│             if text:
   655│                 self.map_text += "\n\n" + text
   656│         return True

   658│     def _ledger_text(self, budget: int) -> str:
   659│         """The ledger (``ledger.select``): within ``budget`` tokens, the lines of the messages that left whose
   660│         names, not in view, are most likely to be needed again."""
   661│         from .ledger import Names, prior, select
   662│         if self._names is None:
   663│             self._names = Names(self.tr)
   664│         t = len(self.msgs)
   665│         self._names.extend(t)
   666│         covered, self._jit_ids = set(), set()
   667│         for mi in self._visible():
   668│             for i in self.fz.by_msg.get(mi, ()):
   669│                 if self.tr.units[i].kind != "thinking":  # thinking is not sent back: its names are not in view
   670│                     covered |= self.tr.units[i].words
   671│             self._jit_ids |= self._jit_lines.get(mi, set())  # lines appended to a message in view stay in view
   672│         for mi, ln, ws in self._pool:
   673│             if (mi, ln) in self._jit_ids:
   674│                 covered |= ws
   675│         head = getattr(self.model, "ledger", None)
   676│         p = {}
   677│         for _, _, ws in self._pool:
   678│             for w in ws:
   679│                 if w not in p and w not in covered and w in self._names.stats:
   680│                     x = self._names.features(w, t)
   681│                     p[w] = self.model.ledger_prob(x) if head is not None else prior(x, self.lerr, self._names.errors(w))
   682│         taken = select(self._pool, p, covered, budget, self.least)
   683│         self._ledger_ids = {(mi, ln) for mi, ln in taken}
   684│         self.stats["ledger_lines"] += len(taken)

   686│             return ""
   687│         where = f" (each message is kept whole in {self._spill_dir}/mNNNNN.md)" if self._spill_dir else ""
   688│         return "\n".join([f"{MARK} Facts from the messages that moved out, the ones most likely to be needed "
   689│                            f"again{where}:"] + [f"m{mi + 1:05d} {ln}" for mi, ln in taken])

   691│     def _call_words(self, i: int) -> frozenset:

   693│         u = self.tr.units[i]
   694│         b = af.blocks(self.tr.msgs[u.msg].get("content"))
   695│         tid = b[u.block].get("tool_use_id") if u.block < len(b) and isinstance(b[u.block], dict) else None
   696│         if not tid:

   699│             for j in self.fz.by_msg.get(mi, ()):
   700│                 cu = self.tr.units[j]
   701│                 if cu.kind == "call":
   702│                     cb = af.blocks(self.tr.msgs[mi].get("content"))
   703│                     if cu.block < len(cb) and cb[cu.block].get("id") == tid:

   707│     def _jit_text(self, t: int) -> None:
   708│         """Just-in-time lines for the request about to be sent: of the lines that left the view, those sharing
   709│         a name with what arrived since the previous model call and holding a name the view lacks, by the
   710│         ledger's worth per token (``ledger.select``), within ``jit`` tokens; appended to the latest message,
   711│         so the prefix before it is untouched and the lines are read from the cache from then on."""
   712│         from .ledger import Names, prior, select
   713│         steps = self.tr.steps
   714│         lo = max(1, steps[-1]) if steps else 0
   715│         latest, covered = set(), set()
   716│         for mi in self._visible():
   717│             for i in self.fz.by_msg.get(mi, ()):
   718│                 u = self.tr.units[i]
   719│                 if u.kind == "thinking":
   720│                     continue
   721│                 covered |= u.words
   722│                 if mi >= lo:
   723│                     latest |= u.words

1│ """Goal-conditioned context: each request is sent the context of its own goal, not the whole conversation.
     2│ 
     3│ A conversation mixes goals: find a file, fix a script, explain how the Sun burns. The agent's next step
     4│ needs what its current goal produced (the request, what was tried, what came back) and almost never what
     5│ the other goals did; carrying them costs tokens on every request and gives the model more to be
     6│ distracted by. The unit above the paragraph is therefore the *turn* (a request of the person and the
     7│ agent's work on it), and the turns that serve one goal form a *thread*.
     8│ 
     9│ Links. When a request arrives, the probability that its turn will draw on each earlier turn ``j`` is
    10│ estimated from what is known at that moment::
    11│ 
    12│     p(n -> j) = sigma(f(x_nj))
    13│ 
    14│ ``x_nj`` says how much of the request's information turn ``j`` holds (the IDF-weighted share of the
    15│ request's words found there, in the person's own words there, and the share of the request's names:
    16│ paths, files, identifiers, values), whether ``j`` is the previous turn or belongs to the thread in
    17│ progress, how long ago it was, how many of the request's names were never seen before (a new directory or
    18│ file is a new goal) and how short the request is (a bare "run it again" leans on the previous turn). ``f`` is the additive logistic model of the chunk heads, trained
    19│ on recorded sessions with labels from hindsight: turn ``n`` drew on turn ``j`` when an action in ``n``
    20│ copied a distinctive token whose source was in ``j`` (``hindsight``). No labelling by hand. Until a link
    21│ head has been trained, a fixed prior stands in.
    22│ 
    23│ Threads. A turn joins the thread of the turn it most probably draws on::
    24│ 
    25│     k* = thread(argmax_j p(n -> j))    if  max_j p(n -> j) >= link,   else a new thread
    26│ 
    27│ (the maximum, not the probability of drawing on any turn of the thread: that one grows with the number
    28│ of turns, and the longest thread would absorb every request).
    29│ Threads only grow (a turn never moves to another), which is what makes them cacheable.
    30│ 
    31│ The view. For a request in thread ``A`` the model is sent the anchor (the first message), the turns of
    32│ ``A`` in their order and, in the first message of every turn where the conversation came (back) to ``A``,
    33│ one card per other thread, frozen when that turn was first sent: what was asked, what was done, which
    34│ files changed, the last answer, in a few lines. Inside ``A`` the learned engine works as before
    35│ (paragraphs scored by the ``keep`` head, removed by rent or buy) and whatever outside ``A`` the request
    36│ names is brought back by the index and the ``soon`` head (``engine``).
    37│ 
    38│ Why this shape and not a fresh selection at every request: providers cache prefixes. A thread's view only
    39│ grows at its end, so every request inside a thread reads it from the cache; coming back to a thread sends
    40│ a prefix the provider has seen before (DeepSeek keeps prefixes for hours), and leaving one costs nothing:
    41│ the other thread is simply not sent. A selection made from scratch at every request would change early
    42│ positions and pay most of the context again each time.
    43│ """

    96│     ``decide``: a function (turn index, per-thread probabilities) -> thread, to replace the rule (the
    97│     hindsight threads used to train the link head)."""
    98│ 
    99│     def __init__(self, tr, fz, head: Head | None = None, link: float = 0.15, share: float | None = None,
   100│                  decide=None):
   101│         self.tr, self.fz, self.head, self.link, self.share = tr, fz, head, link, share
   102│         self.turns: list[Turn] = []
   103│         self.members: list[list[int]] = []  # thread -> its turns
   104│         self.last: list[int] = []  # thread -> its latest turn
   105│         self.chosen: list[tuple] = []  # turn -> (thread, its probability, best other probability)
   106│         self.rows: list[tuple] = []  # turn -> [(earlier turn, features)] computed when it opened
   107│         self.decide = decide
   108│         self._m = 0  # messages taken in
   109│         self._df: Counter = Counter()
   110│         self._n = 0

   112│         self._wkey, self._w = None, {}  # the request whose word weights are in _w
   113│ 
   114│     # ------------------------------------------------------------ growth
   115│ 
   116│     def update(self) -> None:
   117│         tr, fz = self.tr, self.fz
   118│         while self._m < len(tr.msgs):
   119│             mi = self._m
   120│             self._m += 1
   121│             us = fz.by_msg.get(mi, ())
   122│             if starts_turn(tr, fz, mi):
   123│                 self._open(mi, us)
   124│             t = self.turns[-1]
   125│             for i in us:
   126│                 t.terms |= fz.terms[i]
   127│                 t.seen |= tr.units[i].words
   128│                 t.tokens += tr.units[i].tokens
   129│                 t.units.append(i)
   130│                 self._df.update(fz.terms[i])
   131│                 self._names |= tr.units[i].words
   132│             self._n += len(us)
   133│ 
   134│     def _open(self, mi: int, us) -> None:
   135│         asked = [i for i in us if self.tr.units[i].kind == "user" and is_request(unit_text(self.tr, i))]
   136│         req = set().union(*(self.fz.terms[i] for i in asked))
   137│         names = set().union(*(self.tr.units[i].words for i in asked))
   138│         n = len(self.turns)
   139│         if not n:
   140│             self.turns.append(Turn(mi, req, names, thread=0))
   141│             self.members.append([0])
   142│             self.last.append(0)
   143│             self.chosen.append((0, 1.0, 0.0))
   144│             self.rows.append([])
   145│             return
   146│         rows = [(j, self.features(req, names, j)) for j in range(n)]
   147│         p = [self.prob(x) for _, x in rows]
   148│         joint = [0.0] * len(self.members)  # per thread: the most probable link to one of its turns
   149│         for (j, _), pj in zip(rows, p):
   150│             k = self.turns[j].thread
   151│             joint[k] = max(joint[k], pj)
   152│         order = sorted(range(len(joint)), key=lambda k: (-joint[k], -self.last[k]))
   153│         best = order[0]
   154│         if self.decide is not None:
   155│             th = self.decide(n, joint)
   156│         else:
   157│             th = best if joint[best] >= self.link else len(self.members)
   158│         if th == len(self.members):
   159│             self.members.append([])
   160│             self.last.append(n)
   161│         self.members[th].append(n)
   162│         self.last[th] = n
   163│         self.turns.append(Turn(mi, req, names, thread=th))
   164│         other = max((joint[k] for k in order if k != th), default=0.0)
   165│         self.chosen.append((th, joint[th] if th < len(joint) else 0.0, other))
   166│         self.rows.append(rows)

   168│     # ------------------------------------------------------------ links
   169│ 
   170│     def idf(self, w: str) -> float:
   171│         return math.log(1 + self._n / (1 + self._df.get(w, 0)))
   172│ 
   173│     def features(self, req: set, names: set, j: int, n: int | None = None) -> list[float]:
   174│         """What is known, when a request arrives (its topic words ``req`` and names ``names``), about whether
   175│         its turn (number ``n``: the next one by default) will draw on turn ``j`` (``LINK_FEATURES``)."""
   176│         n = len(self.turns) if n is None else n
   177│         t = self.turns[j]
   178│         weight = self._weights(req)
   179│         total = sum(weight.values()) or 1.0
   180│         shared = req & t.terms
   181│         s = sum(weight[w] for w in shared)
   182│         asked = sum(weight[w] for w in req & t.request)
   183│         prev = float(j == n - 1)
   184│         return [s / total, math.log1p(s), max((weight[w] for w in shared), default=0.0), asked / total,
   185│                 len(names & t.seen) / len(names) if names else 0.0, prev,
   186│                 float(t.thread == self.turns[n - 1].thread), math.log1p(n - 1 - j),
   187│                 len(names - self._names) / (len(names) + 2), math.log1p(len(req)),  # shrunk: one new name says little
   188│                 prev / (1 + len(req)), math.log1p(t.tokens), float(j == 0)]
   189│ 
   190│     def _weights(self, req: set) -> dict:
   191│         """IDF of the request's words (a word never seen weighs most)."""
   192│         if self._wkey is not req:
   193│             self._wkey, self._w = req, {w: self.idf(w) for w in req}
   194│         return self._w
   195│ 
   196│     def prob(self, x: list[float]) -> float:
   197│         if self.head is not None:
   198│             p, pi = self.head.prob(x), self.share if self.share else 0.5
   199│             return p * pi / (p * pi + (1 - p) * (1 - pi))  # the head was trained balanced
   200│         b, w = PRIOR
   201│         z = b + sum(w.get(f, 0.0) * v for f, v in zip(LINK_FEATURES, x))
   202│         return 1 / (1 + math.exp(-max(-30.0, min(30.0, z))))
   203│ 
   204│     # ------------------------------------------------------------ what the turns hold
   205│ 
   206│     def relevance(self, j: int) -> float:
   207│         """Probability that the turn in progress draws on turn ``j``."""
   208│         n = len(self.turns) - 1
   209│         cur = self.turns[n]
   210│         return self.prob(self.features(cur.request, cur.names, j, n))
   211│ 
   212│     def active(self) -> int:
   213│         return self.turns[-1].thread if self.turns else 0
   214│ 
   215│     def span(self, j: int) -> tuple[int, int]:
   216│         """Messages of turn ``j``: [start, end)."""
   217│         end = self.turns[j + 1].start if j + 1 < len(self.turns) else len(self.tr.msgs)
   218│         return self.turns[j].start, end
   219│ 
   220│     def ask(self, j: int) -> str:
   221│         """What the person asked in turn ``j``, on one line."""
   222│         tr, mi = self.tr, self.turns[j].start
   223│         text = " ".join(unit_text(tr, i) for i in self.fz.by_msg.get(mi, ())
   224│                         if tr.units[i].kind == "user" and is_request(unit_text(tr, i)))
   225│         return _line(text, CARD_ASK)

   227│     def card(self, k: int, fixes=None) -> str:
   228│         """Thread ``k`` in a few lines: deterministic, so the same thread at the same point always gives the
   229│         same bytes."""
   230│         tr, turns = self.tr, [self.turns[j] for j in self.members[k]]
   231│         first = turns[0]
   232│         asked = f'"{self.ask(self.members[k][0])}"'
   233│         if len(turns) > 1:
   234│             asked += (f", … ({len(turns) - 2} more), latest" if len(turns) > 2 else ", then") + \
   235│                 f' "{self.ask(self.members[k][-1])}"'

   238│             for i in t.units:
   239│                 u = tr.units[i]
   240│                 if u.kind == "call":
   241│                     actions.append(_action(tr, i))
   242│                     cat, path, _ = self.fz.info.get(i, ("", None, False))
   243│                     if cat == WRITE and path and path not in changed:
   244│                         changed.append(path)
   245│                 elif u.kind == "text":
   246│                     answer = unit_text(tr, i)

   250│             shown = actions[-CARD_ACTIONS:]
   251│             out += f". Did ({len(actions)}): " + "; ".join(shown) + ("; …" if len(actions) > len(shown) else "")
   252│         # what was changed and which failing tests it made pass (``fixes(j)``: the engine's account of turn j)
   253│         why = "".join(fixes(j) for j in self.members[k]) if fixes else ""
   254│         if changed and not why:
   255│             out += ". Changed: " + ", ".join(changed[-8:])
   256│         if answer:
   257│             out += f'. Last answer: "{_line(answer, CARD_ANSWER)}"'
   258│         return out + "." + why

   260│     def cards(self, limit: int, where=None, fixes=None) -> str:
   261│         """The other threads, the most recently active first (``where(k)``: where thread ``k``'s full text is)."""
   262│         a = self.active()
   263│         others = sorted((k for k in range(len(self.members)) if k != a), key=lambda k: -self.last[k])
   264│         if not others:
   265│             return ""
   266│         lines = [f"{MARK} This conversation has other topics. They are left out so that this request gets the "
   267│                  f"context of its own goal; anything in them can be asked for or looked up again:"]
   268│         lines += [self.card(k, fixes) + (where(k) if where else "") for k in others[:limit]]
   269│         if len(others) > limit:
   270│             lines.append(f"• … and {len(others) - limit} older topics.")
   271│         return "\n".join(lines)

   274│ def _line(text: str, n: int) -> str:
   275│     x = " ".join(text.split())

   279│ def _action(tr, i: int) -> str:
   280│     b = af.blocks(tr.msgs[tr.units[i].msg].get("content"))[tr.units[i].block]
   281│     args = b.get("input") if isinstance(b.get("input"), dict) else {}
   282│     what = next((args[k] for k in ("file_path", "path", "command", "pattern", "url", "query", "description")
   283│                  if isinstance(args.get(k), str)), "")
   284│     return f"{b.get('name', '?')} {_line(what, 70)}".strip()

   289│ class GoalEngine(Engine):
   290│     """The learned engine on the active thread only: the view is the anchor, the thread's turns and the
   291│     frozen cards of the other threads (``link``: probability a request must reach to join a thread;
   292│     ``cards``: other threads described at most)."""
   293│ 
   294│     def __init__(self, model: Model, link: float = 0.15, cards: int = 8, leave: str = "oldest", **params):
   295│         super().__init__(model, **params)
   296│         self._params.update(link=link, cards=cards, leave=leave)
   297│         self.link, self.ncards, self.leave = link, cards, leave
   298│         self.out: set[int] = set()  # turns of a thread moved out of the view at the cap (``leave="turns"``)
   299│         self.goal = Threads(self.tr, self.fz, getattr(model, "link", None), link,
   300│                             model.trained_on.get("link_share"))
   301│         self.frozen: dict[int, str] = {}  # first message of a turn where the thread changed -> cards sent there
   302│         self._vis: tuple | None = None
   303│         self._pos: dict[int, int] = {}
   304│         self._offset: dict[int, int] = {}
   305│         self._carded: dict[int, tuple] = {}
   306│         self._merged: dict[tuple, tuple] = {}
   307│ 
   308│     def add(self, m: dict) -> None:
   309│         super().add(m)
   310│         self.goal.update()
   311│         self._vis = None
   312│ 
   313│     def decide(self, now: float | None = None) -> None:
   314│         g = self.goal
   315│         n = len(g.turns)
   316│         if n > 1 and g.turns[-1].thread != g.turns[-2].thread and g.turns[-1].start not in self.frozen:
   317│             text = g.cards(self.ncards, self._where if self.spill else None,
   318│                            lambda j: self._fixes(*g.span(j), limit=len(self.msgs)))
   319│             if text:
   320│                 self.frozen[g.turns[-1].start] = text
   321│                 self.stats["cards"] += 1
   322│             self.stats["switches"] += 1
   323│         super().decide(now)
   324│ 
   325│     def _where(self, k: int) -> str:
   326│         spans = [self.goal.span(j) for j in self.goal.members[k]]
   327│         files = ", ".join(f"m{a + 1:05d}–m{b:05d}" for a, b in spans[-4:])
   328│         return f" Full text: {self._spill_dir}/ ({files}.md)."
   329│ 
   330│     def _visible(self) -> list:
   331│         key = (len(self.msgs), self.start, len(self.goal.turns), len(self.out))
   332│         if self._vis is not None and self._vis[0] == key:
   333│             return self._vis[1]
   334│         g = self.goal
   335│         if not g.turns:
   336│             out = list(range(len(self.msgs)))
   337│         else:
   338│             out = [0]
   339│             for j in g.members[g.active()]:
   340│                 if j in self.out:
   341│                     continue
   342│                 a, b = g.span(j)
   343│                 out.extend(range(max(a, self.start, 1), b))
   344│         self._vis = (key, out, frozenset(out))
   345│         return out
   346│ 
   347│     def _leave(self, sizes: list[int], target: float | None = None) -> bool:
   348│         """``leave="turns"``: over the cap, whole earlier turns of the thread leave the view, those the turn in
   349│         progress is least likely to draw on first (``Threads.relevance``), until the view is under ``floor`` ×
   350│         ``cap``; the anchor says what was asked in them. Otherwise, or when that is not enough, the oldest
   351│         messages leave (``Engine._leave``)."""
   352│         g = self.goal
   353│         if self.leave != "turns" or len(g.turns) < 2:
   354│             return super()._leave(sizes, target)
   355│         target = self.floor * self.cap if target is None else target
   356│         total = sum(sizes)
   357│         cur = len(g.turns) - 1
   358│         cands = sorted((g.relevance(j), j) for j in g.members[g.active()] if j != cur and j not in self.out)
   359│         moved = []
   360│         for _, j in cands:
   361│             if total <= target:
   362│                 break
   363│             a, b = g.span(j)
   364│             total -= sum(sizes[mi] for mi in range(max(a, 1), b))
   365│             self.out.add(j)
   366│             moved.append(j)
   367│         if not moved:
   368│             return super()._leave(sizes, target)
   369│         self._vis = None
   370│         self.stats["left_turns"] += len(moved)
   371│         asks = [g.ask(j) for j in sorted(self.out)]
   372│         self.map_text = (f"{MARK} Earlier requests of this topic were moved out of the context to keep it small; "
   373│                          f"what they found is brought back when it becomes relevant, marked \"{MARK} recalled\":\n"
   374│                          + "\n".join(f"- {x}" for x in asks[-20:]))
   375│         turns_text = self.map_text
   376│         if total > target and super()._leave(self._sizes(), target):
   377│             self.map_text = turns_text + "\n\n" + self.map_text  # both: the turns moved out and the messages
   378│         return True
   379│ 
   380│     def _out_of_view(self, cid: int) -> bool:
   381│         i, j = self.index.chunks[cid]
   382│         if (i, j) in self.live:
   383│             return False
   384│         if j in self.dropped.get(i, ()):
   385│             return True
   386│         mi = self.tr.units[i].msg
   387│         self._visible()
   388│         return mi != 0 and mi not in self._vis[2]
   389│ 
   390│     def _message(self, mi: int) -> tuple[dict, int]:
   391│         m, size = super()._message(mi)
   392│         card = self.frozen.get(mi)
   393│         if not card:
   394│             return m, size
   395│         hit = self._carded.get(mi)
   396│         if hit is not None and hit[0] is m:
   397│             return hit[1], hit[2]
   398│         out = dict(m, content=af.blocks(m.get("content")) + [{"type": "text", "text": card}])
   399│         hit = (m, out, size + est({"type": "text", "text": card}))
   400│         self._carded[mi] = hit
   401│         return hit[1], hit[2]
   402│ 
   403│     def render(self) -> list[dict]:
   404│         """The visible messages, consecutive ones of the same role joined (the anchor and the request that
   405│         follows it when the turns in between belong to other threads)."""
   406│         out, pos, offset = [], {}, {}
   407│         for mi in self._visible():
   408│             m = self._message(mi)[0]
   409│             if out and out[-1]["role"] == m["role"]:
   410│                 prev = out[-1]
   411│                 hit = self._merged.get((id(prev), id(m)))
   412│                 if hit is None or hit[0] is not prev or hit[1] is not m:
   413│                     joined = dict(prev, content=af.blocks(prev.get("content")) + af.blocks(m.get("content")))
   414│                     hit = (prev, m, joined)
   415│                     self._merged[(id(prev), id(m))] = hit
   416│                 offset[mi] = len(af.blocks(prev.get("content")))
   417│                 out[-1] = hit[2]
   418│             else:
   419│                 out.append(m)
   420│                 offset[mi] = 0
   421│             pos[mi] = len(out) - 1
   422│         self._pos, self._offset = pos, offset
   423│         return out
   424│ 
   425│     def position(self, mi: int) -> int | None:
   426│         return self._pos.get(mi)
   427│ 
   428│     def block_offset(self, mi: int) -> int:
   429│         """Blocks of other messages before message ``mi``'s own in the message that carries it."""
   430│         return self._offset.get(mi, 0)

   448│     """``goal:model=PATH;link=0.15;cards=8;`` and every setting of ``learned:``; what is not given is D's
   449│     (``D_SPEC``). A fixed ``cap`` replaces the economic one."""

   459│ # ------------------------------------------------------------ hindsight: what each turn drew on
   460│ 
   461│ def drew_on(tr, th: Threads) -> list[set]:
   462│     """For each turn, the earlier turns an action in it copied a distinctive token from."""
   463│     import bisect
   464│     starts = [t.start for t in th.turns]
   465│     out = [set() for _ in th.turns]
   466│     for u in tr.units:
   467│         j = bisect.bisect_right(starts, u.msg) - 1
   468│         for s in u.uses:
   469│             n = bisect.bisect_right(starts, s) - 1
   470│             if n > j:
   471│                 out[n].add(j)
   472│     return out
   473│

   475│ def link_rows(tr, fz) -> list[tuple]:
   476│     """Training examples for the link head from one recorded segment: (features, drew on, 1, drew on) for
   477│     every pair of a turn and an earlier turn. The threads the features see are the hindsight ones (a turn
   478│     joins the thread of the latest turn it drew on), as the trained rule will mostly reproduce them."""
   479│     probe = Threads(tr, fz)
   480│     probe.update()
   481│     drew = drew_on(tr, probe)
   482│ 
   483│     def decide(n, joint):
   484│         js = sorted(drew[n])
   485│         return th.turns[js[-1]].thread if js else len(th.members)
   486│     th = Threads(tr, fz, decide=decide)
   487│     th.update()
   488│     rows = []
   489│     for n, pairs in enumerate(th.rows):
   490│         for j, x in pairs:
   491│             y = int(j in drew[n])
   492│             rows.append((x, y, 1, y))
   493│     return rows

   496│ def fit_links(rows) -> Head | None:
   497│     from .learn import fit
   498│     if len(rows) < 30 or not any(r[1] for r in rows) or all(r[1] for r in rows):
   499│         return None
   500│     return fit(rows, n_bins=6, epochs=8)

   503│ def pair_scores(threads: list[int], truth: list) -> tuple[float, float]:
   504│     """(precision, recall) of a grouping of turns against the true one, over pairs of turns: of the pairs
   505│     put in one thread, the share that share a goal; of the pairs that share a goal, the share put together."""
   506│     same_t = same_g = both = 0
   507│     for a in range(len(threads)):
   508│         for b in range(a):
   509│             t, g = threads[a] == threads[b], truth[a] == truth[b]
   510│             same_t += t
   511│             same_g += g
   512│             both += t and g
   513│     return (both / same_t if same_t else 1.0), (both / same_g if same_g else 1.0)

   528│ def interleave(segs: list, seed: int = 0, gap: float = 60.0) -> Segment:
   529│     """One conversation made of several recorded ones: their turns mixed in a random order that keeps the
   530│     order within each, as a person does who goes back and forth between tasks. Every message is real, so
   531│     the hindsight labels hold. Times keep each turn's own pace, with ``gap`` seconds between turns."""
   532│     rnd = random.Random(seed)
   533│     queues = []

   536│         queues.append([(seg[a:b], times[a:b]) for a, b in turns_of(seg)])
   537│     queues = [q for q in queues if q]
   538│     out, out_times, clock = Segment(), [], 0.0
   539│     current = rnd.randrange(len(queues)) if queues else 0
   540│     while any(queues):
   541│         live = [k for k, q in enumerate(queues) if q]
   542│         if current not in live or rnd.random() < 0.5:
   543│             current = rnd.choice(live)
   544│         msgs, times = queues[current].pop(0)
   545│         base = next((x for x in times if x is not None), None)

1│ """Hindsight analysis of recorded agent sessions: how much of the context was ever used.
     2│ 
     3│ Context management is a caching problem. At every step the agent is sent a
     4│ context and produces an action; the question is which pieces of the past it
     5│ needs. Once a session is over its whole future is known, so for each piece
     6│ we can ask whether anything the agent did *afterwards* drew on it. This is
     7│ the context counterpart of Belady's optimal cache policy: the ideal context
     8│ at step t holds exactly what is used at t or later.
     9│ 
    10│ Use is traced lexically ("provenance"). An action (assistant text and tool
    11│ call inputs) uses a piece of context when it contains a distinctive token
    12│ from it: an identifier, a path, a dotted name, a version or a long number,
    13│ such as a file it read and now edits, a name it found with grep, a line it
    14│ copies into an edit, or a value it reports to the user. When several pieces contain the token, the most recent one
    15│ gets the credit. Information used without being copied (an error that
    16│ changed the plan, a rule obeyed by not acting) is not seen, so "never used"
    17│ is an upper bound on what is superfluous, not a proof. Replaying sampled
    18│ steps against a real model is the check for that.
    19│ 
    20│ From the recordings alone (no API calls) it reports:
    21│ 
    22│   * dead weight: the share of the input tokens paid over a session that were
    23│     tool outputs never used again;
    24│   * re-fetches (calls repeated with identical arguments) and stale reads
    25│     (file contents still in context after the file was edited);
    26│   * for each context policy: tokens sent, effective cost with prompt caching,
    27│     peak context and the *miss rate*: of the distinctive tokens the agent
    28│     took from older context (not the latest exchange), the share the policy
    29│     had removed from its view at that moment.
    30│ 
    31│ Policies: ``full`` (what the harness sends), ``clear`` (provider-side
    32│ tool-result clearing, like Anthropic's context editing), ``curator`` (this
    33│ proxy, with any settings) and two hindsight oracles that know the future:
    34│ ``oracle`` (drops whole tool outputs never used again) and ``oracle-lines``
    35│ (keeps only the output lines that are used again); ``oracle-cache`` also
    36│ chooses when to remove under prompt caching (the best schedule, by dynamic
    37│ programming) and ``oracle-rent`` knows what but decides when online, by the
    38│ same rent-or-buy rule as the learned engine. The oracles are not
    39│ achievable; they bound what any curation policy could save.
    40│ 
    41│ With ``CACHE_TTL`` set and recorded times, a request sent after the
    42│ provider's cache expired is paid in full by every policy.

   226│ def _units_of(mi: int, m: dict, tool_names: dict, common: frozenset) -> list[Unit]:
   227│     out = []
   228│     for bi, b in enumerate(af.blocks(m.get("content"))):
   229│         if not isinstance(b, dict):
   230│             continue
   231│         t = b.get("type")
   232│         if m["role"] == "user":
   233│             if t == "text":
   234│                 kind, tool, text = "user", "", b.get("text", "")
   235│             elif t == "tool_result":
   236│                 kind, tool, text = "result", tool_names.get(b.get("tool_use_id"), "?"), af.text_of(b.get("content"))
   237│             else:
   238│                 continue
   239│         else:
   240│             if t == "text":
   241│                 kind, tool, text = "text", "", b.get("text", "")
   242│             elif t == "thinking":
   243│                 kind, tool, text = "thinking", "", b.get("thinking", "")
   244│             elif t == "tool_use":
   245│                 kind, tool, text = "call", b.get("name", ""), flat(b.get("input"))
   246│                 tool_names[b.get("id")] = tool
   247│             else:
   248│                 continue
   249│         tokens, opaque = est(b), _strip_media(b)[1] > 0
   250│         out.append(Unit(mi, bi, kind, tool, tokens, words(text, common), opaque, _saving(kind, b, tokens, opaque)))
   251│     return out

   254│ # Seconds a provider keeps a prompt prefix cached after its last use (0: forever). A request sent
   255│ # after a longer pause finds the cache expired: it is paid in full whatever the policy does, so
   256│ # rewriting the context then costs nothing extra. Anthropic and OpenAI keep it about 5 minutes by
   257│ # default; DeepSeek keeps it on disk for hours.
   258│ CACHE_TTL = 0.0
   259│ 
   260│ 
   261│ def set_cache_ttl(seconds: float) -> None:
   262│     global CACHE_TTL
   263│     CACHE_TTL = max(0.0, float(seconds))
   264│ 
   265│ 
   266│ # Which earlier requests the provider can serve a prefix from. "last": only the previous request (a cache
   267│ # breakpoint that moves with the conversation). "any": every earlier request still within ``CACHE_TTL`` of
   268│ # its last use (DeepSeek caches every prefix on disk; Anthropic keeps each breakpoint's prefix for the TTL).
   269│ # Under "any", a view that goes back to an earlier shape (a thread the conversation returns to) is cached.
   270│ CACHE_MEMORY = "last"
   271│ 
   272│ 
   273│ def set_cache_memory(kind: str) -> None:
   274│     global CACHE_MEMORY
   275│     if kind not in ("last", "any"):
   276│         raise SystemExit(f"cache memory is 'last' or 'any', not {kind!r}")
   277│     CACHE_MEMORY = kind

   280│ class PrefixCache:
   281│     """Every prefix of messages sent so far, as a trie of their canonical forms, with when each was last
   282│     used. ``match`` gives how many leading messages of a new request are cached; ``add`` records it."""
   283│ 
   284│     def __init__(self, ttl: float = 0.0):
   285│         self.root: dict = {}
   286│         self.ttl = ttl
   287│ 
   288│     def match(self, canon: list[str], now: float | None) -> int:
   289│         node, n = self.root, 0
   290│         for c in canon:
   291│             nxt = node.get(c)
   292│             if nxt is None or (self.ttl and now is not None and nxt[1] is not None and now - nxt[1] > self.ttl):
   293│                 break
   294│             node, n = nxt[0], n + 1
   295│         return n
   296│ 
   297│     def add(self, canon: list[str], now: float | None) -> None:
   298│         node = self.root
   299│         for c in canon:
   300│             nxt = node.get(c)
   301│             if nxt is None:
   302│                 nxt = node[c] = [{}, now]
   303│             elif now is not None:
   304│                 nxt[1] = now
   305│             node = nxt[0]
   306│

   308│ def cold_steps(seg: list[dict], tr: "Trace", ttl: float | None = None) -> frozenset:
   309│     """Steps (message indices of model calls) whose request came more than ``ttl`` seconds after the
   310│     previous one, from the segment's recorded times (none known: no step is cold)."""
   311│     ttl = CACHE_TTL if ttl is None else ttl
   312│     times = getattr(seg, "times", None)
   313│     if not ttl or not times:
   314│         return frozenset()
   315│     out, prev = set(), None
   316│     for t in tr.steps:
   317│         at = times[t] if t < len(times) else None
   318│         if at is not None:
   319│             if prev is not None and at - prev > ttl:
   320│                 out.add(t)
   321│             prev = at
   322│     return frozenset(out)
   323│

   325│ def likely_lasts(lengths: list[int], k: int, b: float) -> bool:
   326│     """Whether a segment that has lasted ``k`` model calls probably (median) lasts ``b`` more, judging
   327│     from the lengths of other segments (``lengths`` sorted). With none longer than ``k``: no."""
   328│     i = bisect.bisect_right(lengths, k)
   329│     longer = len(lengths) - i
   330│     if not longer:
   331│         return False
   332│     return len(lengths) - bisect.bisect_left(lengths, k + b) >= longer / 2
   333│

   336│ # even when its action paraphrases it, so it widens the labels the model learns from. Misses (the
   337│ # ground truth of "the agent lacked a detail") are always measured on actions only, so runs with and
   338│ # without it stay comparable. Off by default: many recordings keep only an empty, signed thinking block.
   339│ THINKING_EVIDENCE = False

   342│ def set_thinking_evidence(on: bool) -> None:

   344│     THINKING_EVIDENCE = bool(on)

   347│ class Tracer:
   348│     """Builds the trace one message at a time. What is known after message i depends only on messages
   349│     0..i, so a live proxy that sees the conversation grow and the offline analysis of a finished one
   350│     compute exactly the same thing."""
   351│ 
   352│     def __init__(self, common: frozenset = frozenset(), thinking: bool | None = None):
   353│         self.tr = Trace([], [], [], {}, {}, {})
   354│         self.common = common
   355│         self.thinking = THINKING_EVIDENCE if thinking is None else thinking
   356│         self.latest: dict[str, int] = {}  # word -> index of the latest unit containing it
   357│         self.tool_names: dict = {}
   358│ 
   359│     def add(self, m: dict) -> None:
   360│         tr = self.tr
   361│         mi = len(tr.msgs)
   362│         tr.msgs.append(m)
   363│         units = tr.units
   364│         mu = _units_of(mi, m, self.tool_names, self.common)
   365│         if m["role"] == "assistant" and mi > 0:
   366│             out_words = set().union(*(u.words for u in mu if u.kind in ("text", "call")))
   367│             copied = {w for w in out_words if w in self.latest}
   368│             credited = copied
   369│             if self.thinking:
   370│                 thought = set().union(*(u.words for u in mu if u.kind == "thinking"))
   371│                 credited = copied | {w for w in thought if w in self.latest}
   372│             lr = set()
   373│             for w in credited:
   374│                 u = units[self.latest[w]]
   375│                 if not u.uses or u.uses[-1] != mi:
   376│                     u.uses.append(mi)
   377│                 u.word_use[w] = mi
   378│                 u.word_first.setdefault(w, mi)
   379│                 u.word_uses.setdefault(w, []).append(mi)
   380│                 if u.msg < mi - LONG_RANGE and w in copied:
   381│                     lr.add(w)
   382│             tr.steps.append(mi)
   383│             tr.used[mi], tr.long_range[mi] = copied, lr
   384│         for u in mu:
   385│             tr.at[(u.msg, u.block)] = len(units)
   386│             for w in u.words:
   387│                 self.latest[w] = len(units)
   388│             units.append(u)
   389│ 
   390│ 
   391│ def trace(msgs: list[dict], common: frozenset = frozenset(), thinking: bool | None = None) -> Trace:
   392│     tc = Tracer(common, thinking)
   393│     for m in msgs:
   394│         tc.add(m)
   395│     return tc.tr

   400│ @dataclass
   401│ class Waste:
   402│     steps: int = 0
   403│     input_tokens: int = 0  # summed over steps (what is paid without caching)
   404│     peak: int = 0
   405│     result_tokens: int = 0  # tool output tokens summed over steps
   406│     dead_tokens: int = 0  # ... of which never used at that step or later
   407│     never_used: int = 0  # tool output tokens (counted once) never used at all
   408│     results: int = 0  # tool output tokens (counted once)
   409│     media_tokens: int = 0  # outputs with images/documents, summed over steps (use not traceable)
   410│     refetches: int = 0
   411│     refetches_same: int = 0
   412│     refetch_tokens: int = 0
   413│     stale_tokens: int = 0  # file contents in context after the file was edited, summed over steps
   414│     failed_edits: int = 0
   415│     refetch_after_compact: int = 0  # calls repeated after a compaction (the agent lost what they returned)
   416│     refetch_after_compact_tokens: int = 0
   417│     by_tool: dict = field(default_factory=dict)  # tool -> [tokens summed over steps, dead]
   418│ 
   419│     def add(self, o: "Waste") -> None:
   420│         for k, v in asdict(o).items():
   421│             if k == "by_tool":
   422│                 for t, (a, d) in v.items():
   423│                     cur = self.by_tool.setdefault(t, [0, 0])
   424│                     cur[0] += a
   425│                     cur[1] += d
   426│             elif k == "peak":
   427│                 self.peak = max(self.peak, v)
   428│             else:
   429│                 setattr(self, k, getattr(self, k) + v)

   432│ def waste(tr: Trace, head: int = 0) -> Waste:
   433│     w = Waste(steps=len(tr.steps))
   434│     steps = tr.steps
   435│     after = lambda i: len(steps) - bisect.bisect_right(steps, i)  # noqa: E731  steps strictly after message i
   436│     for u in tr.units:
   437│         n = after(u.msg)
   438│         w.input_tokens += u.tokens * n
   439│         if u.kind != "result":
   440│             continue
   441│         if u.opaque:
   442│             w.media_tokens += u.tokens * n
   443│             continue
   444│         dead = u.tokens * after(max(u.msg, u.last_use))
   445│         w.result_tokens += u.tokens * n
   446│         w.dead_tokens += dead
   447│         w.results += u.tokens
   448│         w.never_used += u.tokens if not u.uses else 0
   449│         cur = w.by_tool.setdefault(u.tool, [0, 0])
   450│         cur[0] += u.tokens * n
   451│         cur[1] += dead
   452│     w.input_tokens += head * len(steps)
   453│     size = head
   454│     pos = 0
   455│     for t in steps:  # context size at each step
   456│         while pos < len(tr.units) and tr.units[pos].msg < t:
   457│             size += tr.units[pos].tokens
   458│             pos += 1
   459│         w.peak = max(w.peak, size)
   460│ 
   461│     seen: dict[str, af.Exchange] = {}
   462│     exs = af.exchanges(tr.msgs)
   463│     for ex in exs:
   464│         key = ex.name + "|" + af.canonical(ex.args)
   465│         if key in seen and ex.result_msg is not None:
   466│             w.refetches += 1
   467│             w.refetch_tokens += len(ex.result_text) // 4
   468│             w.refetches_same += int(seen[key].result_text == ex.result_text)
   469│         seen[key] = ex
   470│         info = classify(ex.name, ex.args)
   471│         if info.kind == WRITE and ex.is_error:
   472│             w.failed_edits += 1
   473│         if info.kind == READ and info.path and ex.result_msg is not None:
   474│             edit = next((e for e in exs[ex.step + 1:] if e.call_msg > ex.result_msg
   475│                          and classify(e.name, e.args).kind == WRITE
   476│                          and classify(e.name, e.args).path == info.path), None)
   477│             unit = tr.at.get((ex.result_msg, ex.result_block))
   478│             if edit is not None and unit is not None:
   479│                 w.stale_tokens += tr.units[unit].tokens * after(edit.call_msg)
   480│     return w
