   483│ # ------------------------------------------------------------ policies
   484│ 
   485│ STUB_TOKENS = 25  # a block holding a one-line placeholder
   486│ FOLD_CHARS = 200  # tool call arguments longer than this are content written by the agent
   487│ 
   488│ 
   489│ def _saving(kind: str, b: dict, tokens: int, opaque: bool) -> int:
   490│     """Tokens an oracle saves by removing this unit (0: it is never removed)."""
   491│     if opaque:
   492│         return 0
   493│     if kind == "result":
   494│         return max(0, tokens - STUB_TOKENS)
   495│     if kind == "thinking":
   496│         return tokens
   497│     if kind == "call" and isinstance(b.get("input"), dict):
   498│         return sum(max(0, len(v) // 4 - STUB_TOKENS) for v in b["input"].values()
   499│                    if isinstance(v, str) and len(v) > FOLD_CHARS)
   500│     return 0
   501│ 
   502│ 
   503│ def _keep_lines(text: str, live: set | None) -> str:
   504│     if not live:
   505│         return f"[{text.count(chr(10)) + 1} lines not used again]"
   506│     lines = text.split("\n")
   507│     kept = [ln for ln in lines if words(ln) & live]
   508│     if len(kept) == len(lines):
   509│         return text
   510│     return "\n".join(kept + [f"[{len(lines) - len(kept)} lines not used again]"])
   511│ 
   512│ 
   513│ def _shrink(u: Unit, b: dict, live: set | None = None) -> dict | None:
   514│     """``b`` without what is not used again (``live``: words still to be used; None: nothing is).
   515│     None means drop the block."""
   516│     if u.kind == "thinking":
   517│         return None if not live else b
   518│     if u.kind == "result":
   519│         if live is None:
   520│             return dict(b, content=f"[{u.tool} output not used again]")
   521│         text = af.text_of(b.get("content"))
   522│         new = _keep_lines(text, live)
   523│         return b if new == text else dict(b, content=new)
   524│     if u.kind == "call":
   525│         args = {k: (_keep_lines(v, live) if isinstance(v, str) and len(v) > FOLD_CHARS else v)
   526│                 for k, v in b["input"].items()}
   527│         return b if args == b["input"] else dict(b, input=args)
   528│     return b
   529│ 
   530│ 
   531│ def _rewrite(msgs: list[dict], fn) -> list[dict]:
   532│     """Copy of ``msgs`` where ``fn(msg_index, block_index, block)`` returns the block to send
   533│     (the same object to keep it, None to drop it)."""
   534│     out = []
   535│     for mi, m in enumerate(msgs):
   536│         content = m.get("content")
   537│         if not isinstance(content, list):
   538│             out.append(m)
   539│             continue
   540│         new = []
   541│         for bi, b in enumerate(content):
   542│             nb = fn(mi, bi, b) if isinstance(b, dict) else b
   543│             if nb is not None:
   544│                 new.append(nb)
   545│         changed = len(new) != len(content) or any(x is not y for x, y in zip(new, content))
   546│         out.append(dict(m, content=new or content) if changed else m)
   547│     return out

   567│ class Clear(Policy):
   568│     """Provider-side tool-result clearing, as in Anthropic's context editing (defaults: trigger
   569│     100k input tokens, keep the last 3 tool results). When the context passes ``trigger``, every
   570│     older tool result is replaced by a placeholder; it then stays cleared and the context grows
   571│     again until the next clearing."""

   573│     def __init__(self, keep: int = 3, trigger: int = 0):
   574│         self.keep, self.trigger = keep, trigger
   575│         self.name = f"clear:keep={keep}" + (f",trigger={trigger}" if trigger else "")
   576│ 
   577│     def views(self, session, seg, tr):
   578│         cleared: set = set()
   579│ 
   580│         def view(t):
   581│             return _rewrite(seg[:t], lambda mi, bi, b: dict(b, content="[tool result cleared]")
   582│                             if (mi, bi) in cleared else b)
   583│         for t in tr.steps:
   584│             v = view(t)
   585│             if est(v) > self.trigger:
   586│                 locs = [(u.msg, u.block) for u in tr.units if u.kind == "result" and u.msg < t]
   587│                 cleared = set(locs[:-self.keep] if self.keep else locs)
   588│                 v = view(t)
   589│             yield t, v

   642│ class OracleCache(Policy):
   643│     """Hindsight with prompt caching: also chooses *when* to remove what is never used again.
   644│ 
   645│     Removing content changes the prefix, so the provider cache is lost from the first changed
   646│     message on and that part is paid in full again. Dynamic programming over the steps at which the
   647│     context is rewritten finds the schedule with the lowest effective cost: the bound for a policy
   648│     that loses nothing the agent used.
   649│     """
   650│ 
   651│     name = "oracle-cache"
   652│ 
   653│     def __init__(self, ratio: float = 0.1, write: float = 1.0, ttl: float | None = None):
   654│         self.ratio, self.write, self.ttl = ratio, write, ttl

   656│     def schedule(self, session: Session, seg: list[dict], tr: Trace) -> list[int]:

   658│         expired is paid in full anyway, so rewriting then costs nothing extra."""

   662│         is_cold = [t in cold for t in steps]

   664│         cum = [0]
   665│         for m in seg:
   666│             cum.append(cum[-1] + est(m))

   668│         units = sorted((max(u.msg, u.last_use), u.msg, u.saving) for u in tr.units if u.saving)
   669│         keys = [k for k, _, _ in units]
   670│         saved, dead_at = [], []  # per step: total saving; dead units by message with prefix sums
   671│         for s in steps:
   672│             dead = sorted((m, sv) for _, m, sv in units[:bisect.bisect_left(keys, s)])
   673│             sums = [0]
   674│             for _, sv in dead:
   675│                 sums.append(sums[-1] + sv)
   676│             saved.append(sums[-1])
   677│             dead_at.append(([m for m, _ in dead], sums))
   678│ 
   679│         def view(i, k):  # context size at step k when the last rewrite was at step i
   680│             return head + cum[steps[k]] - saved[i]
   681│ 
   682│         base = [0] * n  # base[x] = sum over y=1..x of (head + cum[steps[y-1]])
   683│         cbase, ncold = [0] * n, [0] * n  # the same over the cold steps only, and how many there are
   684│         for x in range(1, n):
   685│             base[x] = base[x - 1] + head + cum[steps[x - 1]]
   686│             cbase[x] = cbase[x - 1] + (head + cum[steps[x - 1]] if is_cold[x] else 0)
   687│             ncold[x] = ncold[x - 1] + is_cold[x]
   688│ 
   689│         def appended(i, a, b):  # cost of steps a..b, append-only after a rewrite at i
   690│             if a > b:
   691│                 return 0.0
   692│             warm = rho * (base[b] - base[a - 1] - (b - a + 1) * saved[i]) + om * (cum[steps[b]] - cum[steps[a - 1]])
   693│             # a cold step pays at full price what it would have read from the cache
   694│             return warm + (om - rho) * (cbase[b] - cbase[a - 1] - (ncold[b] - ncold[a - 1]) * saved[i])
   695│ 
   696│         inf = float("inf")
   697│         best, back = [inf] * n, [-1] * n
   698│         best[0] = om * view(0, 0)
   699│         for i in range(n - 1):
   700│             ms, sums = dead_at[i]
   701│             p, first = bisect.bisect_left(keys, steps[i]), inf  # first message that a rewrite would change
   702│             for j in range(i + 1, n):
   703│                 while p < len(units) and keys[p] < steps[j]:
   704│                     first = min(first, units[p][1])
   705│                     p += 1
   706│                 if first == inf:

   708│                 cached = 0 if is_cold[j] else min(head + cum[first] - sums[bisect.bisect_left(ms, first)],
   709│                                                   view(i, j - 1))
   710│                 c = best[i] + appended(i, i + 1, j - 1) + rho * cached + om * (view(j, j) - cached)
   711│                 if c < best[j]:

   713│         total, last = inf, 0
   714│         for i in range(n):
   715│             c = best[i] + appended(i, i + 1, n - 1)
   716│             if c < total:

   724│     def views(self, session, seg, tr):
   725│         rewrites = set(self.schedule(session, seg, tr))
   726│         cut = 0
   727│         for k, t in enumerate(tr.steps):

   729│                 cut = t
   730│ 
   731│             def keep(mi, bi, b, cut=cut):
   732│                 u = tr.units[tr.at[(mi, bi)]] if (mi, bi) in tr.at else None

   739│ class OracleRequest(Policy):
   740│     """Hindsight, ignoring the cache: every request is sent exactly what it uses. ``scope="request"``: a tool

   742│     ``scope="step"``: only at the steps that use it. The person's and the agent's own words stay. It shows
   743│     what selecting from scratch at every request costs once prefixes are cached: it sends far fewer tokens
   744│     and can still cost more, because every change of the selection is paid again from where it starts."""

   772│ def rent_threshold(trust: float, lengths: list[int] | None, k: int, cost: float, rent: float) -> float:
   773│     """How much rent must have been paid before buying (as a multiple of the price): rent or buy with a
   774│     prediction (Purohit, Svitkina and Kumar, 2018). ``rent`` is what keeping the dead tokens costs per
   775│     request, ``cost`` what removing them costs once, so ``cost / rent`` requests is the break-even. With
   776│     ``trust`` = 1 the prediction is ignored (buy once the rent paid equals the price: never more than
   777│     twice the optimum for a fixed price; here the price grows with what is sent after the cut, so the
   778│     guarantee is only of the worst case up to the cap); below 1 buy sooner (``trust`` × price) when the segment is
   779│     predicted to last past the break-even and later (price / ``trust``) when it is not."""
   780│     if trust >= 1 or not lengths or rent <= 0:
   781│         return 1.0
   782│     return trust if likely_lasts(lengths, k, cost / rent) else 1 / trust

   785│ class OracleRent(Policy):
   786│     """Knows *what* is never used again (hindsight) but not *when* the segment ends: rewrites by the same
   787│     online rent-or-buy rule as the learned engine. Between ``oracle-cache`` (knows both) and the learned
   788│     policy (knows neither), it splits the gap into the cost of not knowing the future length and the
   789│     cost of not knowing what will be used.
   790│ 
   791│     Every request that still carries a dead block pays its cached price (the rent). At each request,
   792│     for each cut point ``f`` the rent already paid on the dead blocks from ``f`` on is compared with the
   793│     price of removing them: the rest of the context from ``f`` on, sent again uncached. The cut that
   794│     removes most among those whose rent has reached the price is applied. When the cache has expired
   795│     everything dead goes at once, for free."""

   807│         for m in seg:
   808│             cum.append(cum[-1] + est(m))

   810│         ready = sorted((max(u.last_use + 1, u.msg + self.protect + 1), i) for i, u in enumerate(tr.units) if u.saving)

   812│         gone = []  # (message, tokens saved) of removed blocks, sorted
   813│ 
   814│         def keep(mi, bi, b):
   815│             i = tr.at.get((mi, bi))
   816│             return _shrink(tr.units[i], b) if i in removed else b
   817│ 
   818│         for k, t in enumerate(tr.steps):
   819│             while p < len(ready) and ready[p][0] <= t:
   820│                 pool[ready[p][1]] = 0.0
   821│                 p += 1

   824│                 take = list(pool)

   833│                 bought = (0.0, 0.0)

   840│                     rest = cum[upto] - cum[min(f, upto)] - (gone_sums[-1] - gone_sums[bisect.bisect_left(gone_msgs, f)])

   946│     the agent one more read, not the information."""

   950│     calls, writes, reads = {}, {}, {}

   952│         b = af.blocks(tr.msgs[u.msg].get("content"))[u.block]
   953│         if u.kind == "call":
   954│             info = classify(b.get("name", ""), b.get("input") or {})
   955│             calls[b.get("id", "")] = info
   956│             if info.kind == WRITE and info.path:

   958│         elif u.kind == "result":

   961│                 reads[i] = info.path

   978│ def evaluate_segment(session: Session, seg: list[dict], tr: Trace, pol: Policy, records: list | None = None,
   979│                      seg_no: int = 0, ttl: float | None = None) -> PolicyStats:
   980│     st = PolicyStats(pol.name)
   981│     head = est({"system": session.system, "tools": session.tools})
   982│     cold = cold_steps(seg, tr, ttl)
   983│     prev: list[str] | None = None

   987│

   990│         if hit is not None and hit[0] is m:

   993│         by_obj[id(m)] = (m, c)

   995│     times = getattr(seg, "times", None) or []

   997│     for t, view in pol.views(session, seg, tr):
   998│         canon = [canonical(m) for m in view]
   999│         sizes = []
  1000│         for c, m in zip(canon, view):
  1001│             if c not in size_cache:
  1002│                 size_cache[c] = est(m)
  1003│             sizes.append(size_cache[c])
  1004│         size = head + sum(sizes)
  1005│         cached = 0
  1006│         if prev is not None and t not in cold:
  1007│             n = 0
  1008│             for a, b in zip(prev, canon):
  1009│                 if a != b:
  1010│                     break
  1011│                 n += 1
  1012│             cached = head + sum(sizes[:n])

  1015│                 st.resent += sum(sizes[n:len(prev)])

  1020│                 cached = head + sum(sizes[:n]) if n or t not in cold else 0
  1021│             memory.add(canon, now)

  1023│         prev = canon
  1024│         used, lr = tr.used[t], tr.long_range[t]
  1025│         missed: set = set()
  1026│         if not pol.lossless and used:
  1027│             parts = []
  1028│             for c, m in zip(canon, view):

  1031│                 parts.append(flat_cache[c])

1│ """A tiny learned model of which paragraphs of the past an agent will need, trained on its own sessions.
     2│ 
     3│ The hindsight trace (``hindsight.py``) labels the context at every step: is it
     4│ used at this step or later? That gives training data for free, from any
     5│ recorded session of any harness, with no human labelling.
     6│ 
     7│ The unit of decision is a *chunk*: a paragraph of a tool output (split at
     8│ blank lines, at most ``MAX_CHUNK_LINES`` lines; in a file that is roughly one
     9│ function), or a whole tool call or thinking block. For every chunk the model
    10│ sees only what is known at that moment:
    11│ 
    12│   * about the piece it belongs to: kind and tool, size, age, how often and how
    13│     recently it was used, whether the file was edited or read again since,
    14│     and how many requests the user has made since;
    15│   * about the chunk: size, position, whether it was already used, whether it
    16│     holds an error line;
    17│   * relevance to what is about to be sent: the rare words it shares with the
    18│     latest user request, the latest exchange and the agent's latest text,
    19│     weighted by inverse document frequency (as a search engine would);
    20│   * what the agent's answers echoed: an answer about a stomach ache that
    21│     repeats "stomach" and not "muffins" tells which line of the request it
    22│     drew on. Every answer is matched against the topic words of the context
    23│     (plain words too, not only identifiers), so the chunks the agent keeps
    24│     drawing on stay warm and the ones it never echoes cool down;
    25│   * how new the latest request is: the share of its words never seen before
    26│     in the session (a change of task makes most of the past irrelevant).
    27│ 
    28│ Two heads share these features: ``keep`` (used at this step or later: may it
    29│ be dropped?) and ``soon`` (used within the next ``SOON`` steps: should a
    30│ dropped chunk be brought back now?). Each is additive: every feature is cut
    31│ into a few bins learned from the data and each bin gets a weight (a logistic
    32│ GAM, a few hundred numbers in JSON, pure Python, microseconds per chunk).
    33│ 
    34│ The ``learned`` policy evicts in epochs, like the curator: once enough has
    35│ left the recent window, the chunks that leave it are scored and the low ones
    36│ replaced by a marker; everything before is left byte-identical, so the
    37│ provider cache keeps hitting. Older chunks are re-scored at the same time
    38│ but only removed when the saving pays for re-sending the context after them.
    39│ Recall goes the other way and costs no cache: at every step the dropped
    40│ chunks that the ``soon`` head expects to be needed now (it looks at the
    41│ words of the request being sent) are appended to that request, within a
    42│ token budget. Dropping boldly is safe when what is dropped comes back at the
    43│ moment it is needed.
    44│ """

   108│ def terms(text: str) -> set[str]:
   109│     """Topic words: every word of at least 3 letters (identifiers split at ``_``, ``.``, ``/`` and
   110│     camelCase), lower-cased and cut to 5 characters (a crude stemmer that also works for Spanish:
   111│     ``handler``/``handle``, ``aliviar``/``alivio``), plus the distinctive tokens of ``words``."""
   112│     out = set()
   113│     for tok in _TOKEN.findall(text):
   114│         for part in (_HUMP.split(tok) if not tok.islower() else (tok,)):
   115│             if len(part) < 3 or part.isdigit():
   116│                 continue
   117│             low = part.lower()
   118│             if low not in STOP:
   119│                 out.add(sys.intern(low[:5]))
   120│     return out | words(text)

   145│ def split_paragraphs(text: str, max_lines: int = MAX_CHUNK_LINES) -> list[tuple[int, int]]:
   146│     """Line ranges [start, end) cut at blank lines (line-number prefixes of file viewers ignored)."""
   147│     lines = text.split("\n")
   148│     out, start = [], 0
   149│     for i, line in enumerate(lines):
   150│         blank = not _LINENO.sub("", line, count=1).strip()
   151│         n = i + 1 - start
   152│         if (blank and n >= 4) or n >= max_lines:
   153│             out.append((start, i + 1))
   154│             start = i + 1
   155│     if start < len(lines):
   156│         if out and len(lines) - start < 3:
   157│             out[-1] = (out[-1][0], len(lines))
   158│         else:
   159│             out.append((start, len(lines)))
   160│     return out

   163│ def _block(tr: Trace, i: int) -> dict:

   168│ def unit_text(tr: Trace, i: int) -> str:
   169│     u, b = tr.units[i], _block(tr, i)
   170│     if u.kind == "result":
   171│         return af.text_of(b.get("content"))
   172│     if u.kind == "call":
   173│         return flat(b.get("input"))
   174│     return b.get("text") or b.get("thinking") or ""

   177│ def unit_chunks(tr: Trace, i: int) -> list[Chunk]:
   178│     u = tr.units[i]
   179│     if u.kind != "result":
   180│         return [Chunk(i, -1, -1, u.words, u.saving, 0.0, False, terms(unit_text(tr, i)))]
   181│     lines = unit_text(tr, i).split("\n")
   182│     ranges = split_paragraphs("\n".join(lines))
   183│     out = []
   184│     for k, (a, b) in enumerate(ranges):
   185│         part = "\n".join(lines[a:b])
   186│         out.append(Chunk(i, a, b, words(part), len(part) // 4 + 1, k / max(1, len(ranges) - 1),
   187│                          bool(_ERROR.search(part)), terms(part)))
   188│     return out

   191│ def chunk_label(tr: Trace, c: Chunk, t: int) -> int:

   194│     if c.start < 0:

   196│     return int(any(u.word_use.get(w, -1) >= t for w in c.words))

   201│     u = tr.units[c.unit]

   207│ def turn_until(tr: Trace, fz: "Featurizer", t: int) -> int:
   208│     """The last model call of the turn that step ``t`` belongs to: the one before the person's next request."""
   209│     k = bisect.bisect_right(fz.requests, t)
   210│     end = fz.requests[k] if k < len(fz.requests) else len(tr.msgs)
   211│     j = bisect.bisect_left(tr.steps, end)
   212│     return tr.steps[max(0, j - 1)] if j else t

   216│     k = bisect.bisect_left(tr.steps, t)
   217│     return tr.steps[min(len(tr.steps) - 1, k + SOON - 1)]

   232│ class Featurizer:
   233│     """Features of a chunk at a step, using only what is known at that step. Everything it keeps grows
   234│     with the trace (``extend``), so it serves a finished session and a live one alike."""
   235│ 
   236│     def __init__(self, tr: Trace):

   238│         self.info: dict[int, tuple] = {}  # unit index -> (category, path, is_error)
   239│         self._calls: dict[str, tuple] = {}  # tool_use id -> (category, path)
   240│         self._chunks: dict[int, list[Chunk]] = {}
   241│         self.terms: list[set] = []  # per unit
   242│         self.by_msg: dict[int, list[int]] = {}
   243│         self.requests: list[int] = []  # messages where the person wrote something
   244│         self.answers: list[int] = []  # messages where the agent wrote text
   245│         self.novelty: dict[int, float] = {}  # request message -> share of its words never seen before
   246│         self.echoed: dict[str, list[int]] = {}  # topic word -> assistant messages that wrote it
   247│         self.mentions: dict[str, list[int]] = {}  # distinctive word -> assistant messages that wrote it
   248│         self.cowrites: dict[str, list[tuple]] = {}  # word -> (message, other words written in it), in order
   249│         self._amsg: tuple[int, set] | None = None  # the assistant message being collected
   250│         self._act: tuple | None = None  # (t, base activation by word (filled on demand), spread by word, step)
   251│         self.reads: dict[str, list[int]] = {}
   252│         self.writes: dict[str, list[int]] = {}

   254│         self._df: Counter = Counter()
   255│         self._df_pos = 0  # units counted in _df
   256│         self._ctx: _StepContext | None = None
   257│         self.extend()

   259│     def extend(self) -> range:
   260│         """Takes in the units the trace gained since the last call; returns their indices."""

   262│         for i in range(start, len(tr.units)):
   263│             u = tr.units[i]
   264│             if u.kind in ("call", "result"):
   265│                 b = _block(tr, i)
   266│                 if u.kind == "call":
   267│                     info = classify(b.get("name", ""), b.get("input") or {})
   268│                     self.info[i] = (info.kind, info.path, False)
   269│                     self._calls[b.get("id", "")] = (info.kind, info.path)
   270│                     if info.path and info.kind == WRITE:
   271│                         self.writes.setdefault(info.path, []).append(u.msg)
   272│                 elif b.get("tool_use_id", "") in self._calls:
   273│                     kind, path = self._calls[b.get("tool_use_id", "")]
   274│                     self.info[i] = (kind, path, bool(b.get("is_error")))
   275│                     if path and kind == READ:
   276│                         self.reads.setdefault(path, []).append(u.msg)

   279│             self.by_msg.setdefault(u.msg, []).append(i)

   285│                 self.answers.append(u.msg)

   288│                     lst = self.echoed.setdefault(w, [])
   289│                     if not lst or lst[-1] != u.msg:
   290│                         lst.append(u.msg)
   291│                 if self._amsg is not None and self._amsg[0] != u.msg:
   292│                     self._flush()

   294│                     self._amsg = (u.msg, set())
   295│                 self._amsg[1].update(u.words)

   297│         self._flush()  # a message arrives whole: the last one is complete

   300│     def _flush(self) -> None:
   301│         """Records the names an assistant message wrote: their mentions, and which names it wrote together."""
   302│         if self._amsg is None:
   303│             return
   304│         msg, ws = self._amsg
   305│         self._amsg = None
   306│         ws = sorted(ws)[:60]
   307│         for w in ws:
   308│             self.mentions.setdefault(w, []).append(msg)
   309│             others = tuple(x for x in ws if x != w)
   310│             if others:
   311│                 self.cowrites.setdefault(w, []).append((msg, others))

   313│     def activation(self, t: int) -> tuple[dict, dict]:
   314│         """(ACT-R base-level activation, spreading activation) of the names the agent wrote before step ``t``,
   315│         computed on demand and kept for the step. Base level: ln of the sum over past mentions of
   316│         (steps since)^-DECAY, so frequent and recent names are active, as in human memory (Anderson and
   317│         Schooler, 1991). Spread: the names in the agent's latest message (what it is doing now) and in the
   318│         latest request evoke the names they were written with before, by P(name | cue)."""
   319│         if self._act is not None and self._act[0] == t:
   320│             return self._act[1], self._act[2]
   321│         k = bisect.bisect_left(self.tr.steps, t)
   322│         cues: set = set()
   323│         if k:
   324│             cues |= {w for i in self.by_msg.get(self.tr.steps[k - 1], ()) if self.tr.units[i].kind in ("text", "call")
   325│                      for w in self.tr.units[i].words}
   326│         kr = bisect.bisect_left(self.requests, t)
   327│         if kr:
   328│             cues |= {w for i in self.by_msg.get(self.requests[kr - 1], ()) for w in self.tr.units[i].words}
   329│         spread: dict = {}
   330│         for c in cues:
   331│             ev = self.cowrites.get(c)
   332│             j = bisect.bisect_left(ev, (t,)) if ev else 0
   333│             if not j:
   334│                 continue
   335│             share = 1.0 / j
   336│             for _, others in ev[max(0, j - MAX_MENTIONS):j]:
   337│                 for w in others:
   338│                     spread[w] = spread.get(w, 0.0) + share
   339│         self._act = (t, {}, spread, k)
   340│         return self._act[1], spread
   341│ 
   342│     def _base(self, w: str, t: int) -> float | None:
   343│         memo, k = self._act[1], self._act[3]
   344│         if w in memo:
   345│             return memo[w]
   346│         ms = self.mentions.get(w)
   347│         j = bisect.bisect_left(ms, t) if ms else 0
   348│         val = None
   349│         if j:
   350│             steps = self.tr.steps
   351│             val = math.log(sum((k - bisect.bisect_left(steps, m) + 0.5) ** -DECAY for m in ms[max(0, j - MAX_MENTIONS):j]))
   352│         memo[w] = val
   353│         return val
   354│ 
   355│     def chunks(self, i: int) -> list[Chunk]:
   356│         if i not in self._chunks:
   357│             self._chunks[i] = unit_chunks(self.tr, i)
   358│         return self._chunks[i]

   360│     def _terms_at(self, msg: int, kind: str) -> set:
   361│         return set().union(*(self.terms[i] for i in self.by_msg.get(msg, []) if self.tr.units[i].kind == kind))

   363│     def context(self, t: int) -> _StepContext:
   364│         """Document frequencies grow incrementally: visiting steps in increasing order is cheapest."""
   365│         if self._ctx is not None and self._ctx.t == t:
   366│             return self._ctx
   367│         units = self.tr.units
   368│         if self._df_pos and units[self._df_pos - 1].msg >= t:
   369│             self._df, self._df_pos = Counter(), 0
   370│         while self._df_pos < len(units) and units[self._df_pos].msg < t:
   371│             self._df.update(self.terms[self._df_pos])
   372│             self._df_pos += 1
   373│         idf = _Idf(self._df, max(1, self._df_pos))
   374│         recent = set().union(*(self.terms[i] for m in range(max(0, t - RECENT), t) for i in self.by_msg.get(m, [])))
   375│         k = bisect.bisect_left(self.requests, t)
   376│         req = self.requests[k - 1] if k else -1
   377│         request = self._terms_at(req, "user") if k else set()
   378│         k = bisect.bisect_left(self.answers, t)
   379│         answer = self._terms_at(self.answers[k - 1], "text") if k else set()
   380│         self._ctx = _StepContext(t, recent, request, answer, idf, self.novelty.get(req, 0.0))
   381│         return self._ctx

   383│     def echo(self, c: Chunk, ctx: _StepContext) -> tuple[float, int]:
   384│         """(rarity-weighted words of the chunk that the agent wrote after the chunk appeared,
   385│         last message where it did; -1 if none)."""
   386│         created, t, idf = self.tr.units[c.unit].msg, ctx.t, ctx.idf
   387│         strength, last = 0.0, -1
   388│         for w in c.terms:
   389│             ms = self.echoed.get(w)
   390│             if not ms:
   391│                 continue
   392│             k = bisect.bisect_left(ms, t)
   393│             if k and ms[k - 1] > created:
   394│                 r = idf(w)
   395│                 if r >= RARE_IDF:
   396│                     strength += r
   397│                     last = max(last, ms[k - 1])
   398│         return strength, last

   400│     def vector(self, c: Chunk, ctx: _StepContext) -> list[float]:
   401│         t, u = ctx.t, self.tr.units[c.unit]
   402│         cat, path, err = self.info.get(c.unit, ("", None, False))
   403│         created = self._steps_between(u.msg, t)
   404│         past = [s for s in u.uses if s < t]
   405│         since = self._steps_between(past[-1], t) if past else created
   406│         stale = bool(path) and u.kind == "result" and any(u.msg < w < t for w in self.writes.get(path, []))
   407│         superseded = bool(path) and u.kind == "result" and any(u.msg < r < t for r in self.reads.get(path, []))
   408│         if c.start < 0:
   409│             used = bool(past)
   410│         else:
   411│             used = any(u.word_first.get(w, t) < t for w in c.words)
   412│         idf = ctx.idf
   413│         shared = c.terms & (ctx.request | ctx.recent | ctx.answer)
   414│         strength, last = self.echo(c, ctx)
   415│         return [
   416│             float(u.kind == "result"), float(u.kind == "call"), float(u.kind == "thinking"),
   417│             float(cat == READ), float(cat == WRITE), float(cat == EXEC), float(cat == SEARCH),
   418│             float(cat not in (READ, WRITE, EXEC, SEARCH)),
   419│             float(err), math.log1p(u.tokens), math.log1p(created), math.log1p(len(past)), math.log1p(since),
   420│             float(stale), float(superseded),
   421│             math.log1p(bisect.bisect_left(self.requests, t) - bisect.bisect_right(self.requests, u.msg)),
   422│             math.log1p(c.end - c.start if c.start >= 0 else 0), math.log1p(len(c.words)), c.position,
   423│             c.tokens / max(1, u.tokens), float(used), float(c.error),
   424│             math.log1p(sum(idf(w) for w in c.terms & ctx.request)),
   425│             math.log1p(sum(idf(w) for w in c.terms & ctx.recent)),
   426│             math.log1p(sum(idf(w) for w in c.terms & ctx.answer)),
   427│             max((idf(w) for w in shared), default=0.0),
   428│             math.log1p(strength), math.log1p(self._steps_between(last, t) if last >= 0 else created),
   429│             ctx.novelty,
   430│             *self._memory(c, t),
   431│         ]

   433│     def _memory(self, c: Chunk, t: int) -> tuple[float, float]:
   434│         _, spread = self.activation(t)
   435│         acts = [a for a in (self._base(w, t) for w in c.words) if a is not None]
   436│         return max(acts, default=ACTR_FLOOR), max((spread[w] for w in c.words if w in spread), default=0.0)
   437│ 
   438│     def _steps_between(self, a: int, b: int) -> int:
   439│         return max(0, bisect.bisect_left(self.tr.steps, b) - bisect.bisect_right(self.tr.steps, a))

   442│ class _Idf:
   443│     def __init__(self, df: Counter, n: int):
   444│         self.df, self.n = df, n

   446│     def __call__(self, w: str) -> float:

   450│ def candidates(tr: Trace, t: int, protect: int = 0) -> list[int]:
   451│     """Units an eviction policy may shrink at step t: removable and older than the protected window."""
   452│     return [i for i, u in enumerate(tr.units) if u.saving and u.msg < t - protect]

   455│ def spread(items: list, n: int) -> list:
   456│     """``n`` items evenly spaced over ``items`` (all of them if there are fewer)."""
   457│     if n <= 0 or len(items) <= n:
   458│         return list(items)
   459│     return [items[round(i * (len(items) - 1) / (n - 1))] for i in range(n)] if n > 1 else [items[-1]]

   462│ def stable_pick(segs: list, n: int) -> list:
   463│     """``n`` of the (session, segment) pairs, chosen by a hash of the session id and the segment's
   464│     position in it, in their original order: adding sessions changes the choice only where segments
   465│     enter or leave ``segs``, so results of runs on a growing set of recordings stay comparable."""
   466│     if n <= 0 or len(segs) <= n:
   467│         return list(segs)
   468│ 
   469│     def key(k):
   470│         s, seg = segs[k]
   471│         pos = next((j for j, x in enumerate(s.segments) if x is seg), 0)
   472│         return hashlib.sha1(f"{s.id}#{pos}".encode()).hexdigest()
   473│     return [segs[k] for k in sorted(sorted(range(len(segs)), key=key)[:n])]

   476│ def examples(tr: Trace, protect: int = 0, max_rows: int = 0, seed: int = 0, steps: int = 16, fz=None):
   477│     """(features, used at this step or later, tokens, used within ``SOON`` steps, used before the person's next
   478│     request) for chunks at up to ``steps`` steps."""
   479│     fz = fz or Featurizer(tr)
   480│     rnd = random.Random(seed)
   481│     picked = spread(tr.steps, steps)
   482│     per_step = max(20, max_rows // max(1, len(picked))) if max_rows else 0
   483│     rows = []
   484│     for t in picked:
   485│         chunks = [c for i in candidates(tr, t, protect) for c in fz.chunks(i)]
   486│         if not chunks:
   487│             continue
   488│         if per_step and len(chunks) > per_step:
   489│             chunks = rnd.sample(chunks, per_step)
   490│         ctx, until, turn = fz.context(t), soon_until(tr, t), turn_until(tr, fz, t)
   491│         rows += [(fz.vector(c, ctx), chunk_label(tr, c, t), c.tokens, chunk_soon(tr, c, t, until),
   492│                   chunk_soon(tr, c, t, max(t, turn))) for c in chunks]
   493│     return rows

   496│ def early_examples(tr: Trace, fz: Featurizer | None = None) -> list[tuple]:
   497│     """Examples at the cheapest moment to cut a block: the request after the first one that showed it whole.
   498│     Then only the block itself was ever cached (what follows it is new anyway), so cutting it costs almost
   499│     nothing, and the agent's first reaction to it is known. (features, used at that request or later, tokens,
   500│     the same) for every chunk of every tool output and written content."""
   501│     fz = fz or Featurizer(tr)
   502│     steps, by_cut = tr.steps, {}
   503│     for i, u in enumerate(tr.units):
   504│         if u.saving and u.kind in ("result", "call"):
   505│             j = bisect.bisect_right(steps, u.msg)
   506│             if j + 1 < len(steps):
   507│                 by_cut.setdefault(steps[j + 1], []).append(i)
   508│     rows = []
   509│     for t in sorted(by_cut):
   510│         ctx = fz.context(t)
   511│         for i in by_cut[t]:
   512│             for c in fz.chunks(i):
   513│                 y = chunk_label(tr, c, t)
   514│                 rows.append((fz.vector(c, ctx), y, c.tokens, y))
   515│     return rows

   518│ def mission_changes(tr: Trace, fz: Featurizer) -> list[tuple[float, int]]:
   519│     """(novelty, is a new task) for each request after the first one that is followed by at least two
   520│     steps: a new task when nothing written before the request is used until the next one."""
   521│     out = []
   522│     reqs = fz.requests
   523│     for a in range(1, len(reqs)):
   524│         r, nxt = reqs[a], reqs[a + 1] if a + 1 < len(reqs) else len(tr.msgs)
   525│         if sum(1 for t in tr.steps if r < t < nxt) < 2:
   526│             continue
   527│         drew = any(u.msg < r and any(r < s < nxt for s in u.uses) for u in tr.units)
   528│         out.append((fz.novelty.get(r, 0.0), int(not drew)))
   529│     return out

   532│ # ------------------------------------------------------------ model
   533│ 
   534│ @dataclass
   535│ class Head:
   536│     """Additive logistic model: each feature is binned and every bin has a weight."""
   537│ 
   538│     edges: list = field(default_factory=list)  # per feature: bin thresholds
   539│     w: list = field(default_factory=list)  # per feature: one weight per bin
   540│     b: float = 0.0
   541│ 
   542│     def bins(self, x: list[float]) -> list[int]:
   543│         return [bisect.bisect_right(e, v) for e, v in zip(self.edges, x)]
   544│ 
   545│     def prob(self, x: list[float]) -> float:
   546│         z = self.b + sum(wf[k] for wf, k in zip(self.w, self.bins(x)))
   547│         return 1 / (1 + math.exp(-max(-30.0, min(30.0, z))))
   548│ 
   549│     def signals(self, features: list = FEATURES) -> list[tuple[str, float, str]]:
   550│         """(feature, effect size, direction): the spread between its bins' weights, and which end keeps."""
   551│         out = []
   552│         for name, wf in zip(features, self.w):
   553│             if len(wf) < 2:
   554│                 continue
   555│             out.append((name, max(wf) - min(wf), "higher keeps" if wf[-1] > wf[0] else "higher drops"))
   556│         return sorted(out, key=lambda x: -x[1])
   557│ 
   558│ 
   559│ @dataclass
   560│ class Model:
   561│     keep: Head  # used at this step or later
   562│     soon: Head | None = None  # used within the next SOON steps
   563│     features: list = field(default_factory=lambda: list(FEATURES))
   564│     trained_on: dict = field(default_factory=dict)
   565│     link: Head | None = None  # a request's turn will draw on an earlier turn (``goal``)
   566│     turn: Head | None = None  # used before the person's next request: needed for the request in progress
   567│     early: Head | None = None  # used later, judged right after the agent's first look (``early_examples``)
   568│     ledger: Head | None = None  # a name that may have left the view is taken again later (``ledger.rows``)
   569│ 
   570│     def prob(self, x: list[float]) -> float:
   571│         return self.keep.prob(x)
   572│ 
   573│     def soon_prob(self, x: list[float]) -> float:
   574│         """Probability of use within ``SOON`` steps, corrected for the balanced training (heads are trained
   575│         with positives and negatives weighted equally, so their raw output overstates rare events)."""
   576│         if not self.soon:
   577│             return 0.0
   578│         p, pi = self.soon.prob(x), self.trained_on.get("soon_share", 0.5)
   579│         return p * pi / (p * pi + (1 - p) * (1 - pi))
   580│ 
   581│     def ledger_prob(self, x: list[float]) -> float:
   582│         """Probability that an action takes this name again (corrected for the balanced training, like
   583│         ``soon_prob``): the ledger sums probabilities, so the scale matters, not only the rank."""
   584│         p, pi = self.ledger.prob(x), self.trained_on.get("ledger_share", 0.5)
   585│         return p * pi / (p * pi + (1 - p) * (1 - pi))
   586│ 
   587│     def turn_prob(self, x: list[float]) -> float:
   588│         """Probability of use before the person's next request (corrected like ``soon_prob``); without a
   589│         ``turn`` head, the ``keep`` head."""
   590│         if not self.turn:
   591│             return self.prob(x)
   592│         p, pi = self.turn.prob(x), self.trained_on.get("turn_share", 0.5)
   593│         return p * pi / (p * pi + (1 - p) * (1 - pi))
   594│ 
   595│     def early_prob(self, x: list[float]) -> float:
   596│         """Probability of use later, for a chunk the agent has just seen once (corrected for the balanced
   597│         training); without an ``early`` head, the ``keep`` head."""
   598│         if not self.early:
   599│             return self.prob(x)
   600│         p, pi = self.early.prob(x), self.trained_on.get("early_share", 0.5)
   601│         return p * pi / (p * pi + (1 - p) * (1 - pi))
   602│ 
   603│     def remaining(self, k: int) -> float:
   604│         """Expected number of further steps in a segment that has lasted ``k`` steps, from the lengths
   605│         of the training segments (``k`` itself when none was longer)."""
   606│         longer = [n - k for n in self.trained_on.get("lengths", []) if n > k]
   607│         return sum(longer) / len(longer) if longer else float(k)
   608│ 
   609│     def signals(self) -> list[tuple[str, float, str]]:
   610│         return self.keep.signals(self.features)
   611│ 
   612│     def save(self, path: str) -> None:

   614│         d = {"features": self.features, "trained_on": self.trained_on, "keep": asdict(self.keep),
   615│              "soon": asdict(self.soon) if self.soon else None,
   616│              "link": asdict(self.link) if self.link else None, "link_features": LINK_FEATURES,
   617│              "turn": asdict(self.turn) if self.turn else None, "early": asdict(self.early) if self.early else None,
   618│              "ledger": asdict(self.ledger) if self.ledger else None, "ledger_features": list(NAME_FEATURES)}
   619│         with open(path, "w") as f:

   622│     @classmethod
   623│     def load(cls, path: str) -> "Model":
   624│         if path == "curator-model.json" and not os.path.exists(path):
   625│             path = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), "model.json")  # the model shipped with the package

   632│         from .goal import LINK_FEATURES

   634│         ledger = Head(**d["ledger"]) if d.get("ledger") and d.get("ledger_features") == list(NAME_FEATURES) else None
   635│         return cls(Head(**d["keep"]), Head(**d["soon"]) if d.get("soon") else None, d["features"],
   636│                    d.get("trained_on") or {}, link, Head(**d["turn"]) if d.get("turn") else None,
   637│                    Head(**d["early"]) if d.get("early") else None, ledger)

   639│ 
   640│ def _edges(values: list[float], n_bins: int) -> list[float]:
   641│     distinct = sorted(set(values))
   642│     if len(distinct) <= n_bins:
   643│         return [(a + b) / 2 for a, b in zip(distinct, distinct[1:])]
   644│     qs = sorted(values)
   645│     cuts = {qs[int(len(qs) * k / n_bins)] for k in range(1, n_bins)}
   646│     return sorted(c for c in cuts if c > qs[0])
   647│ 
   648│ 
   649│ def fit(rows, n_bins: int = 8, epochs: int = 5, lr: float = 0.1, l2: float = 1e-4, seed: int = 0,
   650│         label: int = 1) -> Head:
   651│     """SGD on the logistic loss, positives and negatives weighted equally. ``label``: which element
   652│     of each row is the target (1: used later; 3: used soon)."""
   653│     if not rows:
   654│         raise SystemExit("no training examples (sessions too short?)")
   655│     rnd = random.Random(seed)
   656│     sample = rows if len(rows) <= 20000 else rnd.sample(rows, 20000)
   657│     d = len(rows[0][0])
   658│     edges = [_edges([r[0][j] for r in sample], n_bins) for j in range(d)]
   659│     head = Head(edges, [[0.0] * (len(e) + 1) for e in edges], 0.0)
   660│     xs = [head.bins(r[0]) for r in rows]
   661│     ys = [r[label] for r in rows]
   662│     n, pos = len(rows), sum(ys)
   663│     wpos = n / (2 * pos) if pos else 1.0
   664│     wneg = n / (2 * (n - pos)) if n - pos else 1.0
   665│     w = head.w
   666│     order = list(range(n))
   667│     step = 0
   668│     for _ in range(epochs):
   669│         rnd.shuffle(order)
   670│         for k in order:
   671│             step += 1
   672│             eta = lr / math.sqrt(1 + step / n)
   673│             x = xs[k]
   674│             z = head.b + sum(wf[j] for wf, j in zip(w, x))
   675│             p = 1 / (1 + math.exp(-max(-30.0, min(30.0, z))))
   676│             g = (p - ys[k]) * (wpos if ys[k] else wneg)
   677│             head.b -= eta * g
   678│             for wf, j in zip(w, x):
   679│                 wf[j] -= eta * (g + l2 * wf[j])
   680│     return head
   681│ 
   682│ 
   683│ def linear_auc(train_rows, test_rows, epochs: int = 4, lr: float = 0.05, seed: int = 0) -> float:
   684│     """AUC of a plain logistic regression on the same features, as a reference for the additive model."""
   685│     rnd = random.Random(seed)
   686│     n, d = len(train_rows), len(train_rows[0][0])
   687│     mean = [sum(r[0][j] for r in train_rows) / n for j in range(d)]
   688│     std = [math.sqrt(sum((r[0][j] - mean[j]) ** 2 for r in train_rows) / n) or 1.0 for j in range(d)]
   689│ 
   690│     def norm(x):
   691│         return [(v - m) / s for v, m, s in zip(x, mean, std)]
   692│     xs = [norm(r[0]) for r in train_rows]
   693│     ys = [r[1] for r in train_rows]
   694│     pos = sum(ys)
   695│     wpos, wneg = n / (2 * max(1, pos)), n / (2 * max(1, n - pos))
   696│     w, b, order, step = [0.0] * d, 0.0, list(range(n)), 0
   697│     for _ in range(epochs):
   698│         rnd.shuffle(order)
   699│         for k in order:
   700│             step += 1
   701│             eta = lr / math.sqrt(1 + step / n)
   702│             z = b + sum(a * c for a, c in zip(w, xs[k]))
   703│             g = (1 / (1 + math.exp(-max(-30.0, min(30.0, z)))) - ys[k]) * (wpos if ys[k] else wneg)
   704│             b -= eta * g
   705│             for j in range(d):
   706│                 w[j] -= eta * g * xs[k][j]
   707│     return auc([b + sum(a * c for a, c in zip(w, norm(r[0]))) for r in test_rows], [r[1] for r in test_rows])
   708│ 
   709│ 
   710│ def auc(scores: list[float], labels: list[int]) -> float:
   711│     """Probability that a random positive scores above a random negative."""
   712│     pairs = sorted(zip(scores, labels))
   713│     pos = sum(labels)
   714│     neg = len(labels) - pos
   715│     if not pos or not neg:
   716│         return float("nan")
   717│     rank_sum, i = 0.0, 0
   718│     while i < len(pairs):
   719│         j = i
   720│         while j < len(pairs) and pairs[j][0] == pairs[i][0]:
   721│             j += 1
   722│         avg = (i + j + 1) / 2  # ranks are 1-based; ties share the average rank
   723│         rank_sum += avg * sum(lbl for _, lbl in pairs[i:j])
   724│         i = j
   725│     return (rank_sum - pos * (pos + 1) / 2) / (pos * neg)
   726│ 
   727│ 
   728│ THRESHOLDS = (0.1, 0.3, 0.5, 0.7, 0.9)
   729│ 
   730│ 
   731│ def risk_threshold(model, rows, risk: float) -> float:
   732│     """The threshold below which a share ``risk`` of the chunks that were needed again score: dropping what
   733│     scores below it loses about that share of what will be needed (Neyman-Pearson: fix the loss, take all
   734│     the saving it allows). Calibrated on ``rows`` (the training examples)."""
   735│     pos = sorted(model.prob(r[0]) for r in rows if r[1])
   736│     if not pos:
   737│         return 0.0
   738│     return pos[min(len(pos) - 1, int(risk * len(pos)))]
   739│ 
   740│ 
   741│ def evaluate(model, rows) -> dict:
   742│     scores = [model.prob(r[0]) for r in rows]
   743│     labels = [r[1] for r in rows]
   744│     out = {"rows": len(rows), "auc": auc(scores, labels), "tokens": sum(r[2] for r in rows),
   745│            "needed": sum(labels)}
   746│     auto = model.trained_on.get("threshold") if hasattr(model, "trained_on") else None
   747│     out["thresholds"] = sorted(set(THRESHOLDS) | ({round(auto, 3)} if auto else set()))
   748│     for thr in out["thresholds"]:
   749│         drop = [(r[1], r[2]) for s, r in zip(scores, rows) if s < thr]
   750│         out[f"thr{thr}"] = {"dropped_tokens": sum(tok for _, tok in drop),
   751│                             "dropped_needed": sum(1 for y, _ in drop if y),
   752│                             "dropped": len(drop)}
   753│     return out

   758│ class Learned(Policy):
   759│     """The online engine (``engine.Engine``) driven step by step over a recorded segment: drops the chunks
   760│     the ``keep`` head scores below ``threshold`` when doing so pays under prompt caching, keeps the
   761│     messages under ``cap`` tokens and, with ``recall``, appends to each request the dropped chunks whose
   762│     probability of use within ``SOON`` steps (``soon`` head) is at least ``recall``, up to ``budget``
   763│     tokens per request."""
   764│ 
   765│     def __init__(self, model: Model, threshold: float = 0.3, protect: int = 6, check: int = 4000,
   766│                  recall: float = 0.0, budget: int = 1500, ratio: float = 0.1, horizon: int = 10,
   767│                  margin: float = 1.0, shortlist: int = 40, cap: int = 0, floor: float = 0.6, rank: str = "soon",
   768│                  rule: str = "rent", trust: float = 1.0, every: int = 4, ttl: float = 0.0, birth: str = "",
   769│                  stub: str = "plain", head: str = "keep", miss: int = 0, early: float = 0.0, spill: str = "",
   770│                  terms: int = 24, cold: int = 0, eoq: int = 0, ledger: int = 0, least: float = 0.0005,
   771│                  name: str = ""):
   772│         self.params = dict(threshold=threshold, protect=protect, check=check, recall=recall, budget=budget,
   773│                            ratio=ratio, horizon=horizon, margin=margin, shortlist=shortlist, cap=cap, floor=floor,
   774│                            rank=rank, rule=rule, trust=trust, every=every, ttl=ttl, birth=birth, stub=stub, head=head,
   775│                            miss=miss, early=early, spill=spill, terms=terms, cold=cold, eoq=eoq, ledger=ledger,
   776│                            least=least)
   777│         self.model = model
   778│         self.recall = recall if model.soon else 0.0
   779│         self.name = name or f"learned:threshold={threshold}" + (f";recall={recall}" if self.recall else "") + \
   780│             (f";cap={cap}" if cap else "")
   781│         self.stats: Counter = Counter()
   782│ 
   783│     @property
   784│     def recalled_chunks(self) -> int:
   785│         return self.stats["recalled_chunks"]
   786│ 
   787│     @property
   788│     def recalled_tokens(self) -> int:
   789│         return self.stats["recalled_tokens"]
   790│ 
   791│     def engine(self):
   792│         from .engine import Engine
   793│         return Engine(self.model, **self.params)
   794│ 
   795│     def views(self, session, seg, tr):
   796│         from .hindsight import est
   797│         eng = self.engine()
   798│         eng.head_tokens = est({"system": session.system, "tools": session.tools})
   799│         times = getattr(seg, "times", None) or []
   800│         for t in tr.steps:
   801│             for m in seg[len(eng.msgs):t]:
   802│                 eng.add(m)
   803│             yield t, eng.view(times[t] if t < len(times) else None)
   804│         self.stats.update(eng.stats)
   805│

   807│ def parse_learned(spec: str) -> Learned:
   808│     """``learned:model=PATH;threshold=0.3;recall=0.05;budget=1500;protect=6;check=4000;ratio=0.1;horizon=10;
   809│     margin=1;cap=0;rank=soon;rule=rent;trust=1;every=4;ttl=0;birth=squeeze+telegraph``"""
   810│     _, _, rest = spec.partition(":")
   811│     kv = dict(x.split("=", 1) for x in filter(None, rest.replace(";", ",").split(",")))
   812│     model = Model.load(kv.pop("model", "curator-model.json"))
   813│     types = {"protect": int, "check": int, "budget": int, "horizon": int, "shortlist": int, "cap": int,
   814│              "every": int, "miss": int, "terms": int, "cold": int, "eoq": int, "ledger": int, "rank": str, "rule": str,
   815│              "birth": str, "stub": str, "head": str, "spill": str}
   816│     return Learned(model, **{k: types.get(k, float)(v) for k, v in kv.items()}, name=spec)

   819│ # ------------------------------------------------------------ tweezers: what to bring back for a request
   820│ 
   821│ WINDOW = 6  # messages: the tweezers look beyond the recent window
   822│ TWEEZER_BUDGETS = (500, 1000, 2000, 4000)
   823│ TWEEZER_METHODS = ("recency", "words", "learned")
   824│ 
   825│ 
   826│ def tweezers(tr: Trace, model: Model, steps: int = 30, window: int = WINDOW, budgets=TWEEZER_BUDGETS,
   827│              rerank: int = 200, fz: Featurizer | None = None) -> dict:
   828│     """At steps where the agent used details from tool outputs or written content older than the recent
   829│     window, the share of those details (distinctive tokens) found in the old chunks each method picks
   830│     for the request being sent, within each token budget:
   831│ 
   832│       * ``recency``: the most recent old chunks first (what a longer window would keep);
   833│       * ``words``: BM25 between the chunk and the request being sent (the latest user request, the
   834│         latest exchange, the agent's latest text): retrieval as in RAG;
   835│       * ``learned``: the ``rerank`` best by ``words``, re-ordered by the ``soon`` head.
   836│     """
   837│     fz = fz or Featurizer(tr)
   838│     pickable = [i for i, u in enumerate(tr.units) if u.saving and u.kind != "thinking"]
   839│     need_at: dict[int, set] = {}
   840│     for i in pickable:
   841│         u = tr.units[i]
   842│         for w, uses in tr.units[i].word_uses.items():
   843│             for s in uses:
   844│                 if u.msg < s - window:
   845│                     need_at.setdefault(s, set()).add(w)
   846│     out = {"steps": 0, "needed": 0, "found": {m: [0] * len(budgets) for m in TWEEZER_METHODS}}
   847│     for t in spread(sorted(need_at), steps):
   848│         need = need_at[t]
   849│         old = [c for i in pickable if tr.units[i].msg < t - window for c in fz.chunks(i)]
   850│         if not old:

   908│ def fill(order: list[int], items: list[Chunk], budget: int) -> list[int]:
   909│     """The items taken greedily in ``order`` while they fit in ``budget`` tokens."""
   910│     taken, used = [], 0
   911│     for k in order:
   912│         n = items[k].tokens
   913│         if used + n <= budget:
   914│             used += n
   915│             taken.append(k)
   916│             if used >= budget:
   917│                 break
   918│     return taken

   921│ def _fill(order: list[int], items: list[Chunk], budget: int) -> set:
   922│     """Words of the items ``fill`` takes."""
   923│     return set().union(*(items[k].words for k in fill(order, items, budget)))

   926│ def _cover(need: set, items: list[Chunk]) -> list[int]:
   927│     """Greedy weighted set cover: the items holding ``need``, most new words per token first."""
   928│     left = set(need)
   929│     cand = {k for k, c in enumerate(items) if c.words & left}
   930│     order = []
   931│     while left and cand:
   932│         k = max(cand, key=lambda k: (len(items[k].words & left) / max(1, items[k].tokens), -k))
   933│         if not items[k].words & left:
   934│             break
   935│         order.append(k)
   936│         left -= items[k].words
   937│         cand.discard(k)
   938│     return order

   941│ def _expected_cover(items: list[Chunk], p: list[float], limit: int) -> list[int]:
   942│     """Greedy for a submodular objective under a token budget: the expected number of distinct details
   943│     kept. A chunk is worth its probability of use times the share of its details that the chunks already
   944│     taken do not hold, per token; the same output read twice, or a paragraph repeated in a later one, is
   945│     worth nothing the second time. Gains only shrink as chunks are taken, so stale heap entries are just
   946│     re-scored (lazy greedy). The order stops once it holds ``limit`` tokens; the rest follow by
   947│     probability per token."""
   948│     def gain(k):
   949│         c = items[k]
   950│         if not c.words:
   951│             return 0.0
   952│         return p[k] * len(c.words - covered) / len(c.words) / max(1, c.tokens)
   953│     covered: set = set()
   954│     heap = [(-gain(k), k) for k in range(len(items))]
   955│     heapq.heapify(heap)
   956│     order, taken, used = [], set(), 0
   957│     while heap and used < limit:
   958│         g, k = heapq.heappop(heap)
   959│         fresh = gain(k)
   960│         if heap and fresh < -heap[0][0] - 1e-12:
   961│             heapq.heappush(heap, (-fresh, k))
   962│             continue
   963│         if fresh <= 0:
   964│             break
   965│         order.append(k)
   966│         taken.add(k)
   967│         covered |= items[k].words
   968│         used += items[k].tokens
   969│     return order + sorted((k for k in range(len(items)) if k not in taken), key=lambda k: -p[k] / max(1, items[k].tokens))

  1015│                   "soon": sorted(newest, key=lambda k: -soon[k]),
  1016│                   "soon/tok": sorted(newest, key=lambda k: -soon[k] / max(1, items[k].tokens)),

  1022│ def budget_bench(tr: Trace, model: Model, steps: int = 16, budgets=BUDGETS, window: int = WINDOW,
  1023│                  fz: Featurizer | None = None) -> dict:
  1024│     """The *what* on its own, without cache economics. At sampled steps the content of the history (tool
  1025│     outputs and written content, in paragraphs) must fit in a budget of tokens, while the rest of the
  1026│     conversation (requests, the agent's text, its calls) stays. Of the distinctive tokens the agent took
  1027│     at that step from content (and that the rest of the conversation does not also hold), the share
  1028│     found in what each method keeps:
  1029│ 
  1030│       * ``recency``: the newest content first (a sliding window: what a small model's harness does);
  1031│       * ``words``: BM25 between the content and the request being sent;
  1032│       * ``keep`` / ``soon``: the model's heads (used again at all / within ``SOON`` steps);
  1033│       * ``soon/tok``: the ``soon`` head per token (the greedy answer to the knapsack);
  1034│       * ``cover``: the ``soon`` head per token, discounted by what the chunks already taken hold
  1035│         (``_expected_cover``);
  1036│       * ``oracle``: hindsight, the fewest tokens that hold what is used (greedy set cover).
  1037│ 
  1038│     Also measured: the content the oracle needs for nothing to be missing at the step, all the content
  1039│     there is, and the size of the rest of the conversation."""
  1040│     nb = len(budgets)
  1041│     out = {"steps": 0, "needed": 0, "needed_far": 0, "cover": [], "content": [], "rest": [],
  1042│            "found": {m: [0] * nb for m in BUDGET_METHODS}, "found_far": {m: [0] * nb for m in BUDGET_METHODS},
  1043│            "complete": {m: [0] * nb for m in BUDGET_METHODS}}
  1044│     for t, need, items, orders, rest_tokens, cover_tokens in budget_steps(tr, model, steps, budgets, fz):
  1045│         far = {w for w, m in need.items() if m < t - window}
  1046│         out["steps"] += 1

1│ """The ledger: the facts of what left the view, kept in a template the anchor carries.
     2│ 
     3│ When messages leave the view (at a rewrite, when the request is sent anew from that point anyway), the names
     4│ they held (paths, identifiers, values, hosts) only come back by a call that reads them again. A few of them
     5│ will be needed: a name the agent typed, one that came back several times, one a request named. The ledger
     6│ keeps, within a budget of tokens, the lines of the messages that left whose names are most likely to be used
     7│ again, each with the message it came from (and the file that keeps it, with ``spill``). It is rebuilt only
     8│ when the view is rewritten, so it never costs the cache anything; between two rewrites it is read at the
     9│ cached price like the rest of the view.
    10│ 
    11│ Which lines: each name ``w`` has a probability ``p(w)`` that a later action takes it (``Names.features``,
    12│ learned from the person's own sessions by hindsight: self-supervised, like the other heads). A line is worth
    13│ the sum of ``p`` over the names it holds that are not already in view or in a line taken before; lines are
    14│ taken by worth per token, greedily (a lazy greedy over a heap). The worth of a set of lines is a weighted
    15│ coverage: monotone and submodular, so the greedy by worth per token comes within ``1 - 1/e`` of the best set
    16│ for the budget less one line (the standard knapsack argument: a line is at most ``LINE_CHARS`` characters,
    17│ about 60 tokens of a budget of thousands, so what the rounding can lose is one line's worth), while a line's
    18│ worth per token is at least ``least`` and the budget lasts.
    19│ """

1│ """Curation policy for Messages API requests.
     2│ 
     3│ Rules:
     4│   * Only tool *results* are ever shortened. System prompt, tool definitions,
     5│     user-written text and assistant turns (including thinking blocks) are
     6│     sent exactly as the harness wrote them. Messages are never removed, so
     7│     every tool_use keeps its tool_result.
     8│   * The most recent ``keep_recent`` tool exchanges are always untouched.
     9│   * Compaction happens in epochs. Once a prefix of the conversation has been
    10│     compacted it is frozen and re-sent byte-for-byte on every later request,
    11│     so provider prompt caching keeps hitting. A new epoch starts only when the
    12│     uncompacted tail grows past ``epoch_tokens``.
    13│   * Before anything else, tool outputs go through the mechanical squeezer
    14│     (stage 1, ``mechanical.py``). It is deterministic, so a squeezed output
    15│     is byte-identical on every request.
    16│   * When a small local model is configured (stage 2, ``mini.py``), elided
    17│     outputs are replaced by the digest it prepared in the background instead
    18│     of a few key lines. Digests are only read at epoch time, never awaited.
    19│   * Loops are handled by ``guard.py``: repeated text in earlier assistant
    20│     messages is removed before it is re-sent, and loop notes are added.
    21│   * Facts the model needs but cannot see are added by ``recall.py``.
    22│   * When an epoch freezes old messages it also folds the large contents the
    23│     agent wrote through tools (the files are on disk) and drops old thinking
    24│     blocks, so the context stays bounded however long the run gets.
    25│   * Annotations (loop notes, recalled context, the periodic progress ledger) are
    26│     appended to the newest user message and then re-sent identically on every

    12│ ``content`` blocks); the engine takes in what it has not seen, and ``view``
    13│ is what to send for the next model call; ``memory`` is everything the engine
